This page explains what a committee/group email address is and how to use it.

If you are a participant using a personal email (Gmail, Yahoo, etc.), this page is for you.

Short Answer

Send committee-wide messages from your own email account to the committee/group mailing-list address.

When you email that address, your message goes to all current participants.

Why This Is Useful

  • You send one email to everyone without typing each person's address.
  • Group correspondence is archived separately for record-keeping.
  • New participants receive future group messages; ask the chair for earlier correspondence they need. Joining does not deliver the past email archive to a personal inbox.

What This Address Is For

  • Send updates to the whole committee/group
  • Ask the whole group a question
  • Share meeting notes or next steps with everyone
  • Keep group communication in one place

What This Address Is Not For

  • Private one-to-one conversations
  • Sensitive information that should only go to staff or leadership
  • File attachments that belong in SharePoint long term

For long-term files, upload to the committee SharePoint Documents library first. Email the committee site address from Quick Links, folder and file name. Follow the SharePoint screenshot guide; do not use Share or Copy link for the external-member handoff.

Which Email Address Should I Use To Send?

Use your own email account: your personal email or your requested SHHA mailbox, whichever the office added to the group.

You do not log in directly to the group address as a mailbox.

The group address is a distribution address, not a personal account.

Quick Decision Flow

  1. Need everyone in the committee/group to see this? Use the committee/group mailing-list address.
  2. Need only one person to see this? Email that person directly.
  3. Sharing a document people will keep working on? Put it in the committee SharePoint Documents library and email the committee site address, folder and file name to the committee/group address.

FAQ

"Should we use this as the preferred email address for the committee/group?"

Yes. Use it for group-wide communication.

"Can we send mail from this address?"

No. Participants should send from their own email account to the group address.

"Do I need to use Teams because Microsoft mentioned Teams in invitation emails?"

No. External volunteers should use email and SharePoint links.

If Microsoft emails mention Teams, that is default wording and can be ignored for this workflow.

  • Volunteer without SHHA Email

For office staff and IT administrators keeping SHHA’s files organized. Start in your work OneDrive’s My files view and read the full folder name before saving or moving anything. Volunteers using personal email should follow the SharePoint screenshot guide and open their committee site in a browser.

Short Version

Every committee has two official places for committee-related materials:

  • An Office folder for staff-facing committee work.
  • A SharePoint folder/site for committee, volunteer, Board, and shared working materials.

Keep this folder structure in place. Committee SharePoint folders belong to their Microsoft 365 groups. The Office workspace belongs to Anna’s user account and has separately managed access for the two office members and one administrator only. Keep that Office access manually curated; do not extend it to committee members or change its ownership.

Keep office-only notes, staff administration and work that is not ready for the committee in the Office workspace, organized under the appropriate existing topic. Do not put it in the committee’s SharePoint library simply because both folders appear in OneDrive.

Recognize the folder pairs in OneDrive

For office and admin users: open your work OneDrive and select My files. The recent-file list is useful for yesterday’s work; My files shows where things belong.

Office and admin users: select My files to find the established folder structure. Select the picture to enlarge it.

Read the complete name. Board - Office and Board - Sharepoint serve different readers. The same pattern appears for other committees, such as C&P and CS&M.

Read the whole folder name. Office and Sharepoint are separate locations for different readers. The small arrow on each icon marks a shortcut. Select the picture to enlarge it.

FolderOwnership and accessPut these files here
Committee - SharepointOwned by the committee’s Microsoft 365 group. Its OneDrive shortcut shows the same files as the committee’s SharePoint Documents library.Committee-facing work: agendas, minutes, reports and reference material the committee should use.
Committee - Office and the Office workspaceAnna’s user-owned OneDrive storage. Access stays manually managed for the two office members and one administrator.Office working files and internal committee-support work for those office/admin users.

The little arrow on a folder icon marks a shortcut: it opens the original shared location. It is not a separate copy or backup. Files in the committee’s SharePoint shortcut stay in sync with SharePoint; changes and deletions affect the shared files.

Check the location after opening a folder

The path across the top shows which folder you opened. This example is the group’s SharePoint location:

Board - Sharepoint opens the group’s shared document location. It shows the same files as the Board SharePoint Documents library. Select the picture to enlarge it.

This example is the separate Office location. Keep its existing office/admin access; do not share this workspace with the committee.

Board - Office is the separate Office workspace. Keep its manually managed office/admin access in place. Select the picture to enlarge it.

Keep files in their proper places

  1. Decide who needs the file. Committee members need the SharePoint folder. Office-only work belongs in the Office workspace.
  2. Open the existing committee and topic folder. Check the name in the path at the top before saving or uploading.
  3. Use a clear file name. Include the topic and date when useful, for example 2026-11-20 Meeting notes. Keep related files together.
  4. Keep one current working file. Avoid scattering copies across the desktop, email and unrelated OneDrive folders.
  5. Ask before reorganizing shared records. Do not casually rename or move the top-level folder pairs, replace shortcuts with copies, change ownership or broaden Office access. Contact IT Help if the structure looks wrong.

Sharing A File With The Board Or A Committee

Do not use Share or Copy link as the file handoff for external Board or committee members. Use the committee site address, folder and file name; see the screenshot guide. Instead, move the file into the SharePoint folder that belongs to that group. Access comes from membership in the group's SharePoint/Microsoft 365 group.

This matters because many Board and committee members use personal email addresses, such as Gmail. Access depends on approved site and document permissions, not an email suffix. Copying a link points to a file; it does not by itself give its recipient permission. External members should access group files through the appropriate SharePoint site.

File-Sharing Decision Flow

Who needs the file?Where should it go?What should you do?
Office staff onlyBoard - Office or the matching committee Office folderMove the file there. This is internal office working space.
Board members, including members using personal email addressesBoard - SharePointMove the file there. Board members open it from the Board SharePoint page.
Committee members, including members using personal email addressesThe matching committee - SharePoint folder/document libraryMove the file there. Members open it from their committee SharePoint site.

The Reliable Board Workflow

  1. Find the file in OneDrive or the Office folder.
  2. Move it into Board - SharePoint.
  3. Tell Board members to open the Board SharePoint page and locate the file.
  4. If helpful, email the Board the folder name and file name. Do not use Share to create separate individual permissions.

Remember: Board - Office is for office staff work. Board - SharePoint forms the Board SharePoint document library and is the correct place for files Board members need to access.

The advantage of this slightly peculiar Microsoft arrangement is a clear separation between files intended for a specific group and files intended for general internal office use. The disadvantage is that Microsoft has once again made a folder name carry the emotional weight of a small policy manual.

Why This Matters

The goal is boring in the best possible way: people should know where things are.

When committee files live in predictable places:

  • Staff can find the current working file without asking three people.
  • Volunteers and committee members can use the same SharePoint links over time.
  • Board members can review materials without hunting through personal folders.
  • Role transitions are less painful because files are not trapped in one person's OneDrive.
  • The committee record stays coherent.

What Belongs In Committee Folders

Use the committee Office folder or SharePoint folder for:

  • Meeting materials
  • Minutes and agendas
  • Committee reports
  • Working drafts that the committee needs
  • Reference documents
  • Photos or supporting materials for committee work
  • Files that future committee members should be able to find

Keep the committee’s shared record in its group-owned SharePoint folder. An Office draft may stay in the Office workspace until it is ready for committee use; the only copy of a committee document should not remain on a desktop or in an email attachment.

What Should Live Somewhere Else

Use the restricted Office workspace, with appropriate internal folders, for:

  • Office-only working notes
  • Staff-only administration files
  • Personnel or confidential documents
  • One-off issues that are not part of the committee record
  • Drafts that are not ready to share with the committee
  • Separate projects that should not clutter the committee folder

If in doubt, ask: “Will a future committee chair, staff member, or Board member reasonably expect to find this in the committee record?” If yes, use the committee folder. If no, use a separate workspace.

Documents Shared With Board

To help preserve institutional knowledge and make important committee information easier to find, each committee SharePoint site now contains a folder called Documents Shared with Board.

These folders are linked from the Board SharePoint site, so Board members can access committee reference materials from a single location.

This area is for documents that should be available to Board members but are not necessarily appropriate for public distribution. Useful examples include:

  • Legal analyses
  • Committee procedures
  • Information related to ongoing disputes or projects
  • Committee charters
  • Resident welcome materials
  • Other enduring reference documents

At launch, these folders may be empty. Committee chairs should add useful files as they identify them. Office staff can also assist.

In general, use this space for enduring documents that Board members may need to reference months or years later. The goal is to keep important information from being buried in monthly meeting folders or old email threads.

Committee members have read/write access to their committee’s Documents library and can add documents there. Office staff manage the home page, navigation and access.

For the full list of direct links to committee SharePoint sites and document libraries, visit the Quick Links & Directory page and scroll to SharePoint Sites (Committee Document Libraries).

If you encounter issues or have suggestions for improvement, contact Anna or Heidi.

How Committee Members Add Or Remove Files

Committee members can create, upload, edit, move, and delete files within their committee's SharePoint document library. That includes members using SHHA Microsoft accounts and approved external accounts, as long as they are members of the committee's SharePoint/Microsoft 365 group.

To add a file:

  1. Open the committee SharePoint site.
  2. Open the Documents library.
  3. Open the correct folder.
  4. Use Upload for an existing file, or New to create a new Word, Excel, PowerPoint, folder, or other supported file.
  5. Confirm the file appears in the committee folder, not in a personal OneDrive folder.

To edit, move, rename, or delete a file:

  1. Open the file or select it in the Documents library.
  2. Use the toolbar or right-click menu for actions such as Rename, Move to, Copy to, or Delete.
  3. For shared committee materials, prefer Move to over downloading and re-uploading. That keeps version history and links more intact.

Small caution: because committee members have write access, deleting or moving files affects everyone. If a folder looks old but might be part of the committee record, ask before tidying it into oblivion. SharePoint has a recycle bin, but “let's not test the recycle bin today” is usually the happier workflow.

Office Staff: Adding A SharePoint Folder To OneDrive

This shortcut is for internal SHHA users only.

  1. Open the committee SharePoint site.
  2. Open the Documents library.
  3. If the committee shortcut is missing, select Add shortcut to OneDrive or Add shortcut to My files. Do not add a duplicate shortcut.
  4. Confirm the library appears under My files in that user's OneDrive.

Internal office users only: this button connects the existing group library to your own OneDrive view. It does not make a second copy. External volunteers use their committee site in the browser. Select the picture to enlarge it.

The shortcut points to the original group-owned SharePoint library. It does not create a copy. Each internal user must add the shortcut while signed in to their own account.

External committee members should not use OneDrive for committee documents. Members using Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud, or another personal email address must bookmark the committee SharePoint site and work in the Documents library through their browser.

Committee SharePoint Permissions

Each committee SharePoint site is connected to its SharePoint/Microsoft 365 group. Membership in that group controls access to the committee document library.

  • Committee members: Contribute access to Documents. They can create, upload, edit, move, and delete documents.
  • Office staff: Owner / Full Control access. They manage membership, permissions, navigation, and the SharePoint home page.

Committee chairs do not need site-owner access or an @sandiahomeowners.org account to work with documents. Keeping page administration with office staff avoids handing a volunteer an accidental cockpit full of Microsoft switches.

Changes to Microsoft 365 group membership automatically update access to the committee's SharePoint documents.

Group-Owned SharePoint Libraries

Committee SharePoint Documents libraries are owned by the committee's Microsoft 365 group. They are not folders in Anna's personal OneDrive and should not be shared person-by-person.

For IT administrators: Microsoft’s explanation of group-connected site access.

Office staff create or administer the group-connected site and manage membership. Committee members receive document access through group membership. Internal office users may add the Documents library as a OneDrive shortcut; external members use the SharePoint site directly.

Important OneDrive Notes For Office Staff

  • OneDrive shortcuts are only for internal office users with SHHA Microsoft accounts.
  • Each internal user adds the shortcut while signed in to their own account.
  • Do not download and re-upload the library or create a separate copy.
  • Do not rename or move the top-level shortcut casually.
  • External committee members use SharePoint only and should never be given OneDrive instructions.

Office Folder Versus SharePoint Folder

Use the Office workspace in Anna’s user-owned OneDrive for staff-centered committee support work. Keep its manually curated access limited to two office members and one administrator. This is separate from committee-group membership.

Use the SharePoint folder/site for committee-facing materials and documents that volunteers, committee members, Board members, or future role holders need to access.

Check the audience, then choose the folder. Preserve the Office/SharePoint distinction and the existing ownership and access arrangement. Keeping the folders tidy helps the next person find the current file without asking who has the latest attachment.

Related Guides

  • Committee SharePoint Guide for committee members
  • SOP: Create a Committee SharePoint Site for office staff and IT

If Something Looks Wrong

Contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org if:

  • You cannot see a shared folder Anna said she shared.
  • You accidentally made a duplicate copy and are not sure which one is current.
  • A committee folder seems to be missing expected files.
  • A folder appears under the wrong account.
  • OneDrive sync is showing errors.
  • A committee member was added but still cannot access the SharePoint site.

Include the folder name, the account you are signed in with, and a screenshot if possible.

Who this is for: staff and volunteers with approved Reminders access. Start by checking the event in its calendar, then open SHHA Toolbox and choose Reminders.

Sign in with your approved SHHA Microsoft account or invited personal-email identity. An SHHA email suffix is not required. Tool access is separate from sign-in; contact IT Help if the card is Restricted.

Check the event in the right calendar

  1. Board meetings: the Office organizer creates or edits the Teams/Outlook meeting and invites admin@sandiahomeowners.org, including updates and cancellations. That address receives invitations; staff do not maintain duplicate meeting dates there.
  2. GRIT deadlines: staff maintain the selected deadline in SHHA’s public Google calendar and mark it Free so it does not reserve the room. The submission guide maintains the publication deadline policy.
  3. Refresh the calendars in Reminders when needed. The tool imports dates; calendar invitation text does not create or authorize a reminder.

Create and activate a reminder

  1. Open Upcoming emails. List and Mini calendar show email send dates in Mountain time, not just meeting dates. Select an email to inspect its message, recipients, From/reply address and event.
  2. Choose New reminder → Choose event. Select the exact Board meeting, GRIT deadline or other imported event.
  3. Select This occurrence only or Every future occurrence. Set up a recurring series once.
  4. Write the emails and check exact recipients, From/reply address and timing. All-day deadlines need a send time. Check the actual dates across daylight-saving changes.
  5. Select Save draft & review. Read the rendered messages and next actual send dates. A saved draft does not send.
  6. When the preview is correct, select Activate reminder. This authorizes future scheduled sends. Saving later changes returns the setup to draft; review and activate it again.
  7. Use Manage reminders to find drafts, active or paused setups and completed one-time reminders. Use Delivery history to review earlier attempts.

Saved messages and recipient groups are shortcuts copied into a setup. Editing the library later does not silently update existing setups. Review the actual setup before activating it.

If something is wrong

What you seeWhat to check
The event is missing or wrongCheck the source calendar, meeting invitation and latest refresh. Correct dates and cancellations in the calendar that owns them.
No upcoming emailOpen Manage reminders. Confirm a setup exists, is active, has future dates and uses the intended event or series. Importing an event alone creates no email.
Needs attentionRead the status. Failed calendar imports, missing required Teams links or unconfirmed sends can hold delivery. Contact IT Help with the event and status.
A send is unconfirmedAsk IT Help to check Microsoft delivery evidence before arranging another send, so recipients do not receive duplicates.
Access deniedCheck the signed-in identity and approved Reminders access. Receiving reminder emails does not require tool access.

Canceled occurrences do not send. A successful send is not repeated just because the event or wording changes. New approvals cover future sends, not missed historical dates.

For an email-address request, contact office staff. For setup or access problems, contact IT Help.

Return to the Toolbox guide. IT maintainers should use IT Infrastructure and Handover and the private operating guide.

For committee members, Board members and anyone sending them a file, including volunteers who use a personal email address. Office staff arrange access; volunteers use the committee’s shared files in their web browser.

Start here: open your committee site from Quick Links & Directory. Its Documents library is the committee’s shared file cabinet. The pictures below show the buttons to use.

Send people to the site, folder and file

Do not use the file’s Share or Copy link button for external volunteers. Those file-sharing links do not work for SHHA’s external-volunteer handoff. Put the file in the committee’s Documents library, then email the committee site address, folder and file name.

A committee site address is different from a file-sharing link. Use the committee address listed in Quick Links, such as https://shha.sharepoint.com/sites/BOARD/. Do not generate a link from the file’s Share or Copy link controls. The volunteer’s approved committee membership gives them access.

Do not use the Share or Copy link buttons shown here. Send the committee site address from Quick Links, followed by the folder and file name. Select the picture to enlarge it.

Before a new volunteer opens files

  1. Ask office staff to confirm the volunteer’s personal email address is added to the correct committee group. They can use Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud or another personal address.
  2. The volunteer opens SHHA’s Microsoft invitation in that inbox and selects Accept invitation. Follow the invitation and sign-in guide if this is their first visit.
  3. Use that same email address to sign in to SharePoint. An SHHA mailbox is not required for this access.

If the person has not been added or invited, contact office staff. Sending a different file-sharing link will not fix missing committee access.

Open the file using your personal email

  1. Open Quick Links & Directory and select your committee’s SharePoint address.
  2. Sign in with the personal email address that received the SHHA invitation. If another account is already selected, use the option to sign in with the invited account.
  3. Follow Microsoft’s sign-in prompts. If Microsoft emails a one-time passcode, get it from that same inbox and enter it.
  4. Select Documents. Some sites already show Documents on their home page.
  5. Open the folder named in the sender’s message, then select the file name. Bookmark the committee site for your next visit.

1. Open Quick Links and choose your committee’s site address. These are site addresses, not links generated by a file’s Share button. Select the picture to enlarge it.

2. Enter the same personal email address that received your SHHA invitation, then choose Next. The picture is deliberately blank; use your own invited address. Select the picture to enlarge it.

Choose Documents to open the committee’s shared file cabinet. The screenshot shows navigation and controls; private files are outside the picture. Select the screenshot to enlarge it.

Add a file for the committee

  1. Open Documents and the correct folder.
  2. Select Create or upload → Files upload. Some library layouts instead show Upload → Files.
  3. Choose the file from your computer.
  4. Wait for the upload to finish and confirm the file appears.

To create a file directly in SharePoint, select Create or upload and choose Word document, Excel workbook, PowerPoint presentation, or Folder. Some layouts label this menu New.

Choose Files upload for a file already on your computer. Wait until its name appears in the folder. Folder upload adds a whole folder. Select the screenshot to enlarge it.

Send the file location by email

Once the file is in Documents, tell people exactly where to find it:

  1. Copy the committee site address from Quick Links.
  2. Write down the folder and exact file name. This saves the recipient from a treasure hunt.
  3. Email those details to the committee mailing list or the intended volunteer’s personal email. Ask them to open the site, choose Documents and follow the folder names.

The meeting notes are ready.

Open the Board site: https://shha.sharepoint.com/sites/BOARD/

Choose Documents → Minutes → Draft meeting notes.docx.

Sign in with the personal email address that received your SHHA invitation.

The folder and file name above are examples. Replace them with your file’s actual location.

Do not use Share or Copy link for this handoff. Do not grant access file by file or move the committee’s file into a personal OneDrive. Office staff handle membership and access problems.

Use SharePoint in your browser

If you use Gmail, Yahoo, iCloud, or another personal email address, access committee documents only through the committee SharePoint site in your browser.

  • Bookmark the committee SharePoint site.
  • Sign in with the same personal email address that received the SHHA Microsoft invitation.
  • Do not try to add the committee folder to OneDrive.
  • Do not move committee files into a personal OneDrive.

This is the standard SHHA workflow for external committee members. It keeps everyone working from the same group-owned document library.

Email and documents do different jobs

ToolUse it for
Your committee mailing listEmailing everyone in the committee
Your committee SharePoint siteStoring and working on committee documents

Use the direct site and mailing-list links supplied by office staff or listed in Quick Links & Directory.

What committee members can do

Committee members have read/write access to the Documents library. You may:

  • Open and download documents
  • Create folders
  • Upload files
  • Create Word, Excel, or PowerPoint files
  • Edit and rename files
  • Move files within the Documents library
  • Delete files that should no longer be kept

Deleting or moving a file affects everyone, so ask before reorganizing material that may be part of the committee record.

What office staff handle

Contact office staff for:

  • Adding or removing committee members
  • Changes to the SharePoint home page or navigation
  • Permissions changes
  • Help recovering or reorganizing files

The committee chair does not need an @sandiahomeowners.org account or site-owner access to work with documents.

Edit or organize a file

  1. Select the file using the circle beside its name, or right-click it.
  2. Choose Open, Rename, Move to, or Delete.
  3. Use Move to when reorganizing files. Do not download and re-upload a file just to move it.

Documents Shared with Board

Use Documents Shared with Board for enduring reference material Board members may need later, such as procedures, legal analyses, project background, charters, or other non-public reference documents.

If future Board members may need it, do not let it disappear into an old email thread.

Office users: choose the committee’s - Sharepoint folder for a file the committee needs. A file left in - Office is in the separate office workspace. See the folder pictures and organization guide.

If something does not work

If you see Access denied or Request access, first check that you used your invited email address and accepted the invitation. If you still cannot get in, contact office staff or IT Help. Include:

  • The email address used to sign in
  • The SharePoint site or folder being opened
  • The exact error message
  • A screenshot, if possible

Finished? Confirm the file appears in the intended Documents folder, then tell the committee its location. For folder placement, continue to SharePoint Folder Organization. If you see Access denied or cannot find a file, contact office staff or IT Help; do not change sharing permissions to work around it.

Who this is for: neighbors looking for public tools, and staff or volunteers doing approved SHHA work. Choose a public link below, or sign in to see Your toolbox.

Public utilities

  • Membership and Communication Statistics: aggregate totals, communication reach and a one-page report.
  • Neighborhood map: published map layers, legends and neighborhood information.
  • GRIT submissions: submit contributions and photographs; use the submission guide for preparation and deadlines.
  • IT help wiki: read instructions without signing in.

Open Your toolbox

For office staff, committee chairs and volunteers collecting a survey, RSVP, headcount or short poll. Start at forms.google.com. Google Forms is SHHA’s preferred option: Microsoft’s sharing choices can be awkward for people outside the organization. forms.microsoft.com is available when a Microsoft form is needed.

Ask the office to create SHHA forms using sandiahomeowners@gmail.com, the designated Google service account. This keeps the form and results with SHHA when volunteers change. Use the office’s approved sign-in process; do not distribute its password. A committee chair can receive a results link without becoming a form editor.

Keep the three links separate

LinkSend it toWhat it permits
Responder linkPeople filling out the survey or RSVPAnswer and submit the form
Results spreadsheet linkThe requesting chair or anyone authorized to read resultsRead the collected rows; use Viewer access
Form editor linkOnly people authorized to build or administer the formChange questions/settings and access responses

Copy responder link supplies the invitation link. Copying the address from the form editor’s browser bar can send the wrong link. Share the results from the linked Google Sheet, with its own access setting.

1. Create the Google form

  1. Open Google Forms. Check the profile icon to confirm the SHHA service account, then choose Blank form.
  2. Name the file and form clearly, for example Committee picnic RSVP. In the description, explain the purpose, deadline and who to contact.
  3. Add each question. Use Multiple choice for one answer, Checkboxes for several choices, Short answer for a brief response, or Paragraph for comments. Turn on Required only for answers you need.
  4. For an RSVP, useful questions include whether the person will attend and the size of their party. Ask for a name or contact address only when the task needs it.
  5. Use Preview to check wording and choices. The screenshots below use a documentation-only example, not an actual event.

A clearly named example form, one question and the Required switch. All answers in these screenshots are invented samples. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

2. Let the intended audience respond

  1. Open Settings → Responses. For an ordinary public survey that should work without a Google account, leave Limit to 1 response off. That option requires Google sign-in.
  2. If you need email addresses without requiring Google sign-in, set Collect email addresses → Responder input, which asks people to type their address, rather than Verified. Otherwise use Do not collect.
  3. Avoid a file-upload question for a simple public RSVP; uploads require Google sign-in.
  4. Review presentation settings. Leave View results summary off unless every respondent is meant to see the response summaries, including free-text answers. The chair’s results spreadsheet is a separate sharing choice.

For this open example, Collect email addresses is Do not collect and Limit to 1 response is off. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

View results summary is off. Sharing the chair’s results sheet is a separate step. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

3. Publish and share the responder link

  1. Select Publish in the form editor. Review Responders and use Manage if needed to set responder access to Anyone with the link for an open resident/volunteer survey.
  2. Finish publishing. Publishing makes the form available to its selected audience; it does not send an announcement for you unless you choose an invitation/notification option.
  3. Select the chain-link icon labelled Copy responder link at the top of the editor, then select Copy in the popup. You can also open Published → Copy responder link. Use this responder link in the invitation.
  4. Paste it into the announcement email, calendar invitation or approved committee notice. Give it a clear label such as Complete the picnic RSVP, and include the closing date.
  5. Open the copied link in a signed-out or private browser window. Check that the intended respondent can reach the form without requesting editor access. Submit a clearly marked sample answer before launching the real survey, then confirm it appears under Responses.

After publishing, select Published to review the audience. This example accepts responses from Anyone with the link. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

The chain-link icon opens Copy responder link. Select Copy in this popup, then paste the link into your invitation. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

Please complete the picnic RSVP by [date]: [responder link]. This link is for submitting your answer.

4. Connect responses to a spreadsheet

  1. Return to the form editor and open Responses.
  2. Choose Link to Sheets (the green spreadsheet icon). If the menu uses different wording, use More → Select destination for responses.
  3. Choose Create a new spreadsheet and select Create, or deliberately select an existing destination.
  4. Open the linked sheet. Confirm the sample answer appears as a row. Subsequent submissions feed this linked spreadsheet.
  5. Keep this spreadsheet as the continuing results destination. Sending an exported Excel/CSV file creates a snapshot; that attachment will not acquire later responses automatically.

Before a spreadsheet is connected, Responses offers Link to Sheets. After connecting it, this button becomes View in Sheets. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

The first sample submission appears as a row in the linked response spreadsheet. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

5. Share a read-only results link

Yes—the results spreadsheet can have an Anyone with the link → Viewer link. You can send it to a requesting committee chair, including someone without an SHHA account. Viewer permits reading rather than editing; anyone who obtains that link can read the shared spreadsheet.

  1. Open the linked Google Sheet, then select Share at its top right.
  2. Under General access, change Restricted to Anyone with the link when all of the spreadsheet’s contents may be seen by anyone who receives the link.
  3. Set the adjacent role to Viewer. Do not choose Editor merely to make the link open.
  4. Select Copy link, then Done to save/close the sharing dialog.
  5. Send this second link to the chair with a label such as View RSVP results — read only. It is different from the link respondents use.
  6. Test the copied results link in a signed-out/private window. Confirm the rows are visible and you cannot edit them. Submit another sample answer through the responder link and verify that a new row arrives in the same results sheet.

For results suitable for link sharing, choose Anyone with the link and Viewer, then Copy link and Done. The account shown is SHHA’s designated service account. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

Test the results link while signed out: View only appears beside the toolbar, and Sign in remains at the top right. A second sample submission has arrived in the same sheet. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

If results contain private contact details or confidential answers, keep General access → Restricted, add the chair’s email address and choose Viewer instead. Sharing only selected results requires a separate suitable summary; hiding a column is not a way to make its data private from spreadsheet readers.

Do not use File → Share → Publish to web for the ordinary read-only handoff. Use the Share dialog’s access setting. Form access and spreadsheet access are separate: test both links.

Here are the [survey name] results: [results spreadsheet link]. This is the live, read-only results sheet; new submissions will appear here. To submit an answer instead, use [responder link].

Close the form and hand it over

  1. At the deadline, open Published, switch Accepting responses off and save. Check the responder link shows that collection has closed.
  2. Keep the form and linked results sheet under SHHA ownership. Record the form editor location, responder link and results-sheet link in the committee’s approved workspace. Keep private results out of this public wiki.
  3. If an additional administrator needs edit access, grant it deliberately. Someone who only needs results can remain a spreadsheet Viewer.

At the deadline, turn Accepting responses off. It changes to Not accepting responses; select Save and test the responder link. Select a screenshot to enlarge it.

If you use Microsoft Forms

Open forms.microsoft.com with your SHHA Microsoft account. Build and preview the form, then select Collect responses. For an audience that includes personal-email users, select Anyone can respond and copy the response link. Test outside the SHHA sign-in session.

Microsoft separates respondent access, collaboration and results sharing, which can make an external handoff awkward. Collect responses is the submission link; a collaboration link gives broader administration access. For a read-only overview, open Responses Overview → More options for responses → Share a summary link. Anyone holding that summary link can see the summary. A summary is different from the detailed results workbook. For row-by-row results, use Open results in Excel and arrange the workbook’s permitted read access separately; Download a copy creates an offline snapshot. External workbook viewers cannot trigger the Microsoft Forms data refresh, so the owner must check that current responses are available.

Google Forms remains the preferred choice for a new SHHA survey or RSVP with the separate live results-sheet handoff described above.

When a link does not work

  • Respondent is asked for access: check that the form is published, the copied link is the responder link and responder access includes that person.
  • Unexpected Google sign-in: check one-response limits, verified email collection, upload questions and responder restrictions.
  • Chair cannot open results: check the Google Sheet’s own Share setting. Publishing the form does not share its spreadsheet.
  • Results do not update: use the linked sheet rather than an old attachment, and check the form’s response destination is still linked.

Need help? Contact office staff to create or find an SHHA form, or IT Help for access problems. Return to Quick Links & Directory.

Start Here — Find Your Path

Different people need different things from this guide. Find your role below and follow the links.

Who you areStart hereFirst action and next step
Resident updating information or preferencesResident account and preferences guideChoose existing-account sign-in or an account request, then review contact details, GRIT and directory choices.
Resident or visitorPublic utilitiesOpen the dashboard, map or GRIT submission form; no account is needed.

This is the main orientation page for SHHA volunteers. You do not need to be technical to use this guide.

What System Does SHHA Use?

SHHA primarily uses Microsoft 365 for:

  • Committee mailing lists
  • Shared inboxes (officer roles)
  • File storage (SharePoint)
  • Internal collaboration

Microsoft 365 owns Board meeting dates; the staff-selected Google calendar owns GRIT deadlines. Toolbox imports dates. Staff save, review and activate reminder setups in Toolbox; importing an event does not authorize sending.

Do I Need a New Microsoft Account?

If you choose personal-email guest access: use the same email address that received your SHHA invitation. If you request your own SHHA mailbox, office staff arrange a separate licensed SHHA account.

When first added, you receive a Microsoft invitation email and must accept it once. After acceptance you can:

  • Access committee SharePoint files
  • Receive group emails
  • Open shared documents

If access fails, the most common cause is that the original invitation was never accepted.

Committee Mailing Lists (Microsoft Groups)

Each SHHA committee has a mailing list so one address reaches the whole committee.

Typical flow

  1. Committee chair informs office staff.
  2. Office invites volunteer as an external Microsoft user.
  3. Volunteer accepts Microsoft invitation.
  4. Volunteer is added to committee mailing list.
Invitation emails may mention Teams or other services. You can ignore those references.

Committee SharePoint Sites (Where Files Live)

Each committee has a SharePoint site that acts as its long-term file cabinet and working library.

Important: SharePoint navigation through Microsoft menus is often confusing. Use the direct SharePoint links provided in committee materials or this help guide.

File Sharing Rule (Most Important)

Do not try to share files directly with committee groups when members are external users. Instead:

  1. Upload the file to SharePoint.
  2. Note the folder and file name in the committee Documents library.
  3. Email the committee site address from Quick Links, folder and file name to the committee mailing list.

Follow the SharePoint screenshot guide. Do not use Share or Copy link as the handoff for external members; keep the working document in the group library.

Shared Role Inboxes (Officers)

Officer mailboxes stay with the role, not the person. Examples:

  • president@sandiahomeowners.org
  • vicepresident@sandiahomeowners.org
  • secretary@sandiahomeowners.org
  • treasurer@sandiahomeowners.org

Best practice: Reply from the shared role inbox, or CC it, so records are preserved for SHHA business.

Board Materials and Calendar

  • Board materials should be uploaded directly to Board SharePoint.
  • Board reminder setups are reviewed and activated in SHHA Toolbox → Reminders. Edit Board meetings in Outlook or Teams and invite admin@sandiahomeowners.org. GRIT deadlines use the staff-selected Google calendar. Contact office staff or IT Help about missing reminders.

If reminders are missing, contact office staff or ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org.

Record-Keeping and Archive

All committee mailing lists include an archival account (admin@sandiahomeowners.org) for retention.

The archive inbox is not monitored and does not reply.

Where to go next

  • Quick Links & Directory for everyday destinations.
  • FAQ for access and email problems.
  • Committee SharePoint Guide for opening and uploading documents.

Need help? Email IT Help with the address you signed in with, the link you opened and the error message. For membership changes, contact office staff.

Public utilities and staff tools

Use the public utilities guide for statistics, the neighborhood map and GRIT submissions. Quick Links & Directory has the everyday destinations. Staff toolbox functions require Microsoft sign-in and separate access; public tools do not require a toolbox account.

This page is for volunteers who already have an SHHA mailbox and may also have role-based inbox access.

Any SHHA volunteer who wants their own SHHA email address may have one. A personal address such as first.last@sandiahomeowners.org is available to volunteers as well as staff. Volunteers may also keep using personal email for committee messages and approved SharePoint guest access. Ask office staff for your preferred option; see account setup and current license costs.

For an email-address request, contact office staff. For setup or access problems, contact IT Help.

What You Should Use

  • Your SHHA email account for routine communication.
  • Committee mailing lists for group communication.
  • SharePoint links for committee files.

Shared Role Inbox Basics

Only the six officer roles have shared mailboxes: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, and CSC Chair. Other committee chairs and task-force leads do not get shared mailboxes.

An officer may also be included in a committee group using another email address, but shared-mailbox access always uses the officer's SHHA account.

  • Sign in to Outlook with your own licensed @sandiahomeowners.org account.
  • The office grants your account Full Access and Send As.
  • Add the shared mailbox manually in Outlook; it may not appear automatically.
  • Use the role mailbox for official role business, or copy it so the message is archived with the role.

You cannot log in directly to a shared mailbox. It is not a separate person or password; it is a role inbox opened through your own account.

See Microsoft's current instructions for opening and using a shared mailbox in Outlook, and see the FAQ for replying from a role mailbox or adding one that does not appear.

Why The President Has Two Email Addresses

Short version: robin.otten@sandiahomeowners.org is Robin's personal SHHA account. president@sandiahomeowners.org is the President mailbox. One belongs to the person; one belongs to the office.

AddressWhat it isUse it for
robin.otten@sandiahomeowners.org Robin's own SHHA sign-in and personal work account Signing in to Microsoft, opening Outlook/SharePoint, and messages meant specifically for Robin as a person
president@sandiahomeowners.org The shared President inbox Official President business that future Presidents may need to see later

Yes, two inboxes is annoying. Think of it as a key and a filing cabinet: Robin's account is the key that lets her into Microsoft; the President inbox is the filing cabinet that stays with the office when the next President takes over.

This is why SHHA keeps both addresses:

  • Continuity: President email history stays with the President role.
  • Less confusion later: The public address does not change every time the role changes.
  • Record keeping: Important President conversations are not stranded in one person's personal mailbox.
  • Cleaner handoff: IT can give the next President access to the same role inbox.

Simple rule: if it is official President business, use president@sandiahomeowners.org. If it is about Robin personally, use robin.otten@sandiahomeowners.org. If you are not sure, the President inbox is usually the safer mailbox for SHHA business.

File Sharing Rule

For committee documents:

  1. Upload the file to the correct committee SharePoint Documents library.
  2. Use the committee’s site address from Quick Links, then give the folder and exact file name.
  3. Email those details to the committee list or intended volunteer. They open the site using the email address already approved for committee access.

Do not use the file’s Share or Copy link button for external volunteers. Those file-sharing links do not work for SHHA’s external-volunteer handoff. Follow the SharePoint screenshot guide.

Avoid one-off attachments for files that should remain in committee records.

Choose the matching scenario, replace every item in square brackets, delete lines that do not apply, and send the completed message to the new users. These are not internal setup notifications; they tell the recipients that setup is complete and explain what they should do next.

This page is for volunteers who participate using a personal email address. You usually do not need a paid Microsoft license.

Any SHHA volunteer who wants their own SHHA email address may have one. A personal address such as first.last@sandiahomeowners.org is available to volunteers as well as staff. Volunteers may also keep using personal email for committee messages and approved SharePoint guest access. Ask office staff for your preferred option; see account setup and current license costs.

For an email-address request, contact office staff. For setup or access problems, contact IT Help.

First-Time Setup

  1. Look for the SHHA organization invitation. A separate group/Teams message may also arrive; you do not need to wait for two emails.
  2. Open the organization invitation email and click Accept invitation.
  3. Use that same email address when prompted to sign in.
  4. Open your committee SharePoint link from the Quick Links & Directory page.
  5. Confirm you receive committee mailing list messages.

Invitation messages you may receive

1) Organization invitation email (expected but confusing)

The subject is usually similar to "Anna, SHHA invited you to collaborate with SHHA".

The email usually includes:

  • A warning message telling you to proceed only if you trust the sender and organization
  • Sender: Anna, SHHA (anna.levchuk@sandiahomeowners.org)
  • Organization: SHHA
  • Domain: sandiahomeowners.org

This is the important one. Click Accept invitation to activate your access.

After you click Accept invitation, Microsoft may bring you to a page that does not make much sense. This is normal and is just a Microsoft quirk. Use the direct links on the Quick Links & Directory page for useful pages and mailing lists.

2) Optional group or Teams message

You may also get an email with a subject like "You have been added to a team in Microsoft Teams".

This is a default Microsoft message and cannot be customized by SHHA.

For external volunteers, we do not recommend using Teams for SHHA work. Instead, follow the SharePoint links on the Quick Links & Directory page for the groups you are part of.

What You Can Expect

  • You can receive committee group email at your personal address.
  • You can open SharePoint documents you were granted access to.
  • You may see references to Microsoft tools SHHA does not use (safe to ignore).
  • You may receive Teams-related emails even though your normal workflow is email and SharePoint.

Most Common Mistakes

  • Not accepting the invitation — until you do, access will fail.
  • Trying to use Teams instead of opening the committee SharePoint site in your browser.
  • Using the file’s Share or Copy link controls instead of sending the committee site address, folder and file name.
  • Sending attachments when the file belongs in SharePoint.

Correct File Sharing Pattern

  1. Upload the file to the correct committee SharePoint Documents library.
  2. Use the committee’s site address from Quick Links, then give the folder and exact file name.
  3. Email those details to the committee list or intended volunteer. They open the site using the email address already approved for committee access.

Do not use the file’s Share or Copy link button for external volunteers. Those file-sharing links do not work for SHHA’s external-volunteer handoff. Follow the SharePoint screenshot guide.

See the illustrated SharePoint guide for opening, uploading and finding committee files.

Need Help?

Contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org if you cannot access files or receive committee messages.

Welcome to the Board. The good news: there is no secret handshake. The mildly annoying news: Microsoft may still ask you to sign in like there is one.

First action: confirm which email address the office has added to the Board group. You can use personal email with an accepted guest invitation, or request your own SHHA mailbox. Start with the volunteer quick start, then open Board documents.

Short Version

  1. Use the Board SharePoint site for meeting packets, pre-reads, and Board working files.
  2. Read the meeting pre-reads before Board meetings.
  3. You can upload files to the Board SharePoint when you need to share material with the Board.
  4. When Trish asks for agenda items, email her anything you want added about a week before the meeting.
  5. If you cannot open something, contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org and include the link that failed.

Board SharePoint: Where The Board Files Live

The Board SharePoint site is the Board's file cabinet. It is where meeting pre-reads, packets, drafts, and reference files should live.

Direct link: https://shha.sharepoint.com/sites/BOARD/

If Microsoft drops you into a confusing page, do not take it personally. Use the direct link above. It is the front door.

Meeting Pre-Reads

Before a Board meeting, check the Board SharePoint for the meeting materials. These are the pre-reads: the things everyone is expected to look at before the meeting so the meeting can be a meeting, not a dramatic public reading of PDFs.

If a document seems missing, ask Trish or office staff. If the link opens for others but not for you, contact ITHelp.

Uploading Files For The Board

Board members can upload files to the Board SharePoint.

  1. Open the Board SharePoint site.
  2. Open the document library or the folder Trish or the Board is using for that meeting/topic.
  3. Click Upload, then choose your file.
  4. After uploading, send the Board or Trish the Board site address, folder and exact file name. Do not use the file’s Share or Copy link button for external members. Follow the SharePoint screenshot guide.

When in doubt, use a clear file name with the topic and date. Future-you and future-neighbors will appreciate it.

Agenda Items

Trish will usually prompt Board members for agenda items before a meeting. When she does, send her any agenda item you want considered about a week in advance.

A helpful agenda request includes:

  • A short title.
  • Whether the item is for information, discussion, or a decision.
  • The Board site address, folder and exact file name for any background document.
  • Any timing concern, such as "needs a vote this month."

Board Email Basics

  • Use board@sandiahomeowners.org when the whole Board should receive a message.
  • Use your own account for ordinary email and Microsoft sign-in.
  • If you also hold an officer role, use that role inbox for official role business so the history stays with the office.

Quick Help

  • Access denied? Make sure you accepted the Microsoft invitation, then contact ITHelp if it still fails.
  • Cannot find pre-reads? Ask Trish or office staff where that meeting's packet is stored.
  • Unsure where to upload? Ask before creating a new folder. Tidier folders make calmer neighbors.

For office staff recording a property ownership change. Sign in to website administration with your own approved account, then open Association → Addresses → New Ownership.

Use New Ownership only when ownership changes. Add tenants and other residents manually when ownership is unchanged. The website route still contains newoccupancy, but the current button and form are named New Ownership.

1. Choose the property and date

  1. Open New Ownership from the Addresses page. New Address is a different task.
  2. Select the correct existing address. Check the street number, street and unit.
  3. Enter the actual known Occupancy Starts At date. The form initially displays a date; do not assume it is the household's actual start date.
  4. Set Is Member to reflect the resident’s expressed membership intent, as handled by the office. Do not copy a previous household’s flag. For a queued membership request, use the User Queue review and Approved/Denied decision, including SHS coordination and the address update requested by the form. A direct checkbox edit does not show that this review occurred or confirm SHS billing.
  5. Enable Has Secondary Mailing Address only when a separate mailing address applies, then check its details.

Current blank form. The displayed date and switches are examples, not a completed household record.

2. Enter the incoming residents

  1. Enter each person's first name, last name, email and phone when available. Use Add Resident for additional people.
  2. Select the correct role. Existing accounts are matched by email address, as stated on the current form. Check uncertain matches before saving to avoid linking the wrong person.
  3. Keep Directory List Name and Directory List Phone unchecked unless the resident has given permission for the corresponding field.

If usable resident information is not available

Use the placeholder name Resident Resident and an address-based placeholder email such as 123address@fake.fake. Use a distinct placeholder for the property so email matching does not connect unrelated households. This is not a working email address.

Follow up: replace the placeholder name and email with the correct resident information when it arrives. Check the existing property/account association before creating another account. Do not treat a placeholder as a reachable contact, directory consent or evidence of membership.

3. Review delivery and directory choices

  1. For the standard new-ownership setup, enable printed GRIT and select all three lists shown: GRIT e-Delivery, Frequent Updates and Essential Updates Only.
  2. Check name and phone listing consent separately for each person. Email subscription and printed delivery do not imply directory permission.
  3. Check any secondary mailing address and the household’s expressed membership intent.

Blank form showing all three mailing lists selected and directory name/phone unchecked. No ownership record was submitted for this capture.

4. Create and check the ownership record

  1. Review the address, unit, actual date, people, roles, email matches and preferences.
  2. When completing a real approved ownership change, choose Create Ownership and confirm the website accepted it.
  3. Check the resulting property and resident associations. Record follow-up for any Resident Resident placeholder.
  4. Tell residents they can use the Member Area and request form to review their information.

Tenants and residents without an ownership change

Do not use New Ownership. Follow Add a resident or tenant manually. Add every tenant individually and associate each with the right property and role.

Check Welcome Visits

The recorded occupancy start feeds Welcome Visits. Authorized staff or volunteers can refresh its website data and review the incoming household. When a household has no recorded occupancy, link/account dates may supply an estimate; those dates do not prove a move-in date. Do not use New Ownership for a tenant simply to produce a date.

Need help? Contact office@sandiahomeowners.org for resident records and membership, or IT Help for technical access. Return to the Staff guide.

Who this is for

This guide is for homeowners making a tram pass reservation at the office kiosk and office staff who may need to reprint passes or process a refund.

Start the kiosk

Click the link in the kiosk's bookmark bar. It automatically signs in the kiosk's authorized user.

The link is https://www.sandiahomeowners.org/tram-pass-reservations/USERHASH_TOKEN

The USERHASH_TOKEN is set in the .env file.  Please refer to the password document for its current value.

Make a tram pass reservation

  1. Enter your address and last name in the kiosk web form.
  2. Select the date you want to reserve and the number of tram pass tickets, up to eight.
  3. Select Submit the pass reservations.
  4. Follow the prompt to pay at the kiosk terminal.
  5. After payment is complete, the kiosk sends the tram passes to the office printer.

Reprint a tram pass reservation

If a successful reservation did not print, or needs to be reprinted:

  1. Open Reservations in the website's administrative area.
  2. Select the reservation and press Print.

Refund a tram pass reservation

  1. Process the refund in the Square website interface. Refunds cannot be processed on the kiosk or in the website's administrative area.
  2. After issuing the refund, open the reservation in the website's administrative area. Remove the refunded number of tram passes. If all passes are being refunded, delete the reservation instead.

Removing the refunded passes from the website makes them available for other homeowners to reserve.

If the kiosk says it is not connected to Square

Only an authorized website administrator should reconnect the website to Square:

  1. Log in to the website's administrative area.
  2. Open Settings, then select Square settings.
  3. In the access token section, select Authorize or Refresh.
  4. If Square asks you to log in, sign in and select the blue Allow button to authorize the requested permissions.

After reconnecting, return to the kiosk and try again.

Answers for SHHA volunteers, officers, and committee members. Find your question in the sidebar or scroll through the sections below.

Any SHHA volunteer who wants their own SHHA email address may have one. A personal address such as first.last@sandiahomeowners.org is available to volunteers as well as staff. Volunteers may also keep using personal email for committee messages and approved SharePoint guest access. Ask office staff for your preferred option; see account setup and current license costs.

For an email-address request, contact office staff. For setup or access problems, contact IT Help.

I was invited but cannot access files. What is usually wrong?

The most common cause is that the original Microsoft invitation email was never accepted. Until you accept that invitation, Microsoft does not recognize you as an authorized guest, so SharePoint links and group emails will not work.

How to fix it — step by step

  1. Search your email (Gmail, Yahoo Mail, iCloud Mail, etc.) for a message from "Microsoft Invitations" with a subject like "You've been invited to access applications within the Sandia Homeowners organization." Check your Spam / Junk folder — these invitations often land there.
  2. Open the email and click the "Accept invitation" button or link.
  3. Sign in with your personal email address — the same one the invitation was sent to. If you already have a Microsoft account linked to that email, use its password. If not, Microsoft will walk you through creating one (free) or send a one-time passcode.
  4. Review and accept the permissions prompt. Microsoft will ask you to agree that SHHA can see basic profile information (name and email). Click Accept.
  5. Try opening your SharePoint link again. It should now work.

If you cannot find the invitation email or the link has expired, contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org and they can resend it.

Microsoft help: B2B collaboration invitation redemption explains the full invitation-acceptance process.

Do I need a paid Microsoft license?

Usually no. Most SHHA volunteers are added as external guest users in Microsoft 365. Guest access is free.

As a guest you can:

  • Receive committee group emails at your personal email address
  • Open and edit documents shared with you on SharePoint
  • View files in your web browser without installing any software

A volunteer may also request a personal SHHA email address. Each SHHA mailbox needs an appropriate paid license, including an officer’s personal account used to open a shared role mailbox. An email license does not grant administrator rights.

Microsoft help: What is guest access in Microsoft 365 Groups?

Do I need to create a new username or password?

For personal-email guest access: use the same personal email address that received your SHHA invitation (e.g., your Gmail, Yahoo Mail, Outlook.com, or iCloud address).

  • If that email is already a Microsoft account (any @outlook.com, @hotmail.com, or @live.com address, or a personal email you previously registered), sign in with its existing password.
  • If it is not a Microsoft account, Microsoft will either send a one-time passcode by email each time you sign in, or prompt you to create a free Microsoft account.
Microsoft help: How to create a new Microsoft account — only needed if Microsoft asks you to during the invitation process.

Can I share a file directly to the committee mailing list from SharePoint?

For SHHA committee work, put the file in the committee Documents library first. Access depends on approved permissions, not the email suffix. Copying a link and granting access are separate actions.

Do not use Share or Copy link to grant a Board or committee group access. Move the file into the correct group SharePoint document library instead. Access comes from membership in that group's SharePoint/Microsoft 365 group.

  • Board files belong in Board - SharePoint, not Board - Office.
  • Committee files belong in that committee's - SharePoint folder/document library.
  • Members using personal email addresses should open files through the appropriate SharePoint site.

See SharePoint Folder Organization for the decision flow and step-by-step instructions.

How should I tell the committee where a document is?

First put the file in the correct SharePoint document library. A link points people to the file; it does not replace group permissions or make a personal OneDrive file available to external members.

  • One official version. Everyone views and edits the same file — no outdated copies.
  • Less confusion. No multiple versions floating around in different inboxes.
  • Centralized records. The file stays in SharePoint, where future volunteers can find it.
  • No file-size limits. Email attachments can bounce if too large. SharePoint links have no such problem.
Rule of thumb: If a document is SHHA committee business, put it in the committee Documents library and email the committee site address, folder and file name. Do not use Share or Copy link as the external-member handoff; follow the screenshot guide. Only use attachments for quick, one-off items that do not need to be retained.
Microsoft help: External or guest sharing in SharePoint

I have a role mailbox (e.g., president@, treasurer@). Should I reply from my personal inbox?

For SHHA business, always reply from the role mailbox (e.g., president@sandiahomeowners.org), or at minimum CC the role mailbox so the message is saved there.

Role mailboxes stay with the position, not the person. When leadership changes, the next officer inherits the full email history. Replies from your personal inbox are lost to the organization.

How to reply from the role mailbox using Outlook on the web

  1. Go to outlook.office.com and sign in with your SHHA licensed account (your @sandiahomeowners.org address).
  2. In the left sidebar, look under "Shared with me" (or right-click your account name → "Add shared folder or mailbox" → type the role address).
  3. Open the email you want to reply to from the role mailbox's Inbox.
  4. Click Reply. Check the From field — it should show the role address. If not, click From and select the role mailbox.
  5. Compose and click Send.
Microsoft help: Open and use a shared mailbox in Outlook

Why does the President need both president@sandiahomeowners.org and robin.otten@sandiahomeowners.org?

Because one address is for the person and one is for the office. It is a little like having a house key and a clubhouse mailbox. They are related, but they do different jobs.

  • robin.otten@sandiahomeowners.org is Robin's own SHHA account. She uses it to sign in to Microsoft and handle messages meant for her personally.
  • president@sandiahomeowners.org is the shared President inbox. It is for official President business and keeps the history with the role.

The shared President inbox is what lets the next President inherit the useful history instead of starting with an empty mailbox and a hopeful shrug. For official President business, use president@sandiahomeowners.org.

See Why The President Has Two Email Addresses for the fuller explanation.

I cannot see my shared role inbox in Outlook. What should I do?

If the shared mailbox does not appear automatically, try adding it manually:

In Outlook on the web (outlook.office.com)

  1. Sign in with your SHHA @sandiahomeowners.org account.
  2. In the left folder pane, right-click your account name.
  3. Select "Add shared folder or mailbox."
  4. Type the role mailbox address (e.g., cscchair@sandiahomeowners.org) and press Enter.
  5. The shared mailbox should appear under "Shared with me".

In the new Outlook desktop app (Windows or Mac)

  1. Open Outlook → go to Mail.
  2. Right-click your account name in the folder pane.
  3. Select "Add shared folder or mailbox."
  4. Type the role mailbox address and click Add.

If it still does not appear, your account may not have been granted permission yet. Contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org to verify your mailbox permissions.

Microsoft help: Open and use a shared mailbox in Outlook — see "What if it didn't work?"

Where should Board materials be submitted?

Upload directly to the Board's SharePoint site using the direct link from your Board materials or ITHelp.

  1. Open the Board SharePoint link in your web browser.
  2. Navigate to the appropriate folder (e.g., "Meeting Materials", "Agendas").
  3. Click Upload → Files and select the document.
  4. Once uploaded, email the Board mailing list with the Board site address from Quick Links, folder and file name. Do not use Share or Copy link for the external-member handoff.

Only deviate from this if office staff specifically requests materials a different way.

Why am I not getting Board reminder emails?

Board meeting reminders use SHHA Toolbox → Reminders and the Microsoft 365 Board meeting invitation. Staff must review and activate the reminder setup; a calendar event alone does not send email.

  1. Check Spam/Junk and tell office staff which meeting and email address are affected.
  2. Staff should confirm the Board meeting invitation includes admin@sandiahomeowners.org, refresh calendars, then check the active reminder setup, recipients, actual send dates and Delivery history.
  3. If delivery remains unresolved, contact IT Help with the meeting date and missing message details.

Receiving reminders does not require access to the staff tool. See SHHA Reminders.

Where do I log in?

There is no single Microsoft website for everything. Which site you use depends on what you need:

What you need to doWhere to goWho uses it
Open committee files Your committee's SharePoint link (from your chair or ITHelp). You can also browse Quick Links & Directory for the correct site All volunteers
