Tip: Most volunteers just click a SharePoint link someone emailed them. You do not need to remember a general login page.
Microsoft help: Sign in to Microsoft 365

Do I have an official SHHA email address? How do I use it?

It depends on your role:

  • Most committee volunteers do NOT have an @sandiahomeowners.org email address. You use your personal email and receive committee emails there. No special login is needed.
  • Only the six officer roles (President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, and CSC Chair) have shared role mailboxes. Other committee chairs use their own account and committee mailing list. See role mailboxes and accessing shared inboxes above.
  • Staff members have full licensed @sandiahomeowners.org accounts and log in at outlook.office.com.

Not sure which category you fall into? Ask your committee chair or email ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org.

Can I forward my SHHA role mailbox email to my personal email?

This is not recommended, and you cannot set it up yourself.

Role mailboxes are shared inboxes managed by the SHHA Microsoft 365 administrator. Only an admin can configure forwarding. It is discouraged because:

  • Replies from your personal inbox will not appear in the role mailbox, breaking record continuity.
  • Forwarded copies persist in your personal inbox after you leave the role.

What to do instead

  • Bookmark outlook.office.com and check the role mailbox regularly.
  • Turn on notifications: in Outlook on the web, click the gear icon (⚙) → View all Outlook settings → General → Notifications → enable email notifications.
  • Use the Outlook mobile app (iOS / Android): sign in with your @sandiahomeowners.org account, then add the shared mailbox.

If you have an exceptional need for forwarding, contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org.

Microsoft help: Add a shared mailbox to Outlook mobile

Can I access my SHHA email from my personal email app (Apple Mail, Gmail app, etc.)?

For the shared role mailbox — generally no. Shared mailboxes cannot be added to third-party email clients like Apple Mail or Gmail. They must be accessed through Microsoft Outlook.

Your best options

  1. Outlook on the web — outlook.office.com in any browser. Nothing to install.
  2. Outlook mobile app — free on iOS and Android. Sign in with your @sandiahomeowners.org account, then add the shared mailbox.
  3. New Outlook desktop app — free on Windows and Mac via outlook.com or your app store.

For regular committee email (external volunteers): Committee emails are delivered directly to your personal inbox. No special setup needed.

Microsoft help: Open and use a shared mailbox in Outlook

How do I see emails going between committee or Board members? Can I see older emails from before I joined?

Committee mailing list emails

  • When someone sends to a committee group address (e.g., csc@sandiahomeowners.org), every current member receives a copy.
  • You can see emails sent from the date you were added onward.
  • You cannot see emails from before you were added. There is no self-service web archive for external members.

If you need prior committee email history

  • Ask your committee chair or a current member to forward key threads.
  • Check the committee's SharePoint document library — important decisions should be saved as files, not just buried in email.
  • The SHHA archive mailbox (admin@sandiahomeowners.org) retains a copy of all group emails. Contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org to request specific messages.

Shared role mailbox emails

If you hold one of the six officer roles, the shared role mailbox retains its full email history regardless of who currently has access. When you are granted access, you can scroll back through all prior sent and received messages — one of the major advantages of using role mailboxes.

How do I send an email to a specific group (Board, committee, or task force)?

For the complete directory of all mailing lists, chair inboxes, and SharePoint URLs, see the Quick Links & Directory page.

Each committee and the Board has a mailing list address. Sending to it delivers to all current members.

GroupEmail address
All Board and committee membersshha-all@sandiahomeowners.org
Board of DirectorsAsk office staff or your chair for the current address
Community Standards Committee (CSC)csc@sandiahomeowners.org
Architectural Control Committee (ACC)acc@sandiahomeowners.org
Other committeesEach has its own @sandiahomeowners.org group address — ask your chair or ITHelp

How to send

  1. Open your email (Gmail, Yahoo Mail, Outlook.com, Outlook on the web — whatever you normally use).
  2. Compose a new message.
  3. In the To field, type the group address (e.g., csc@sandiahomeowners.org).
  4. Write your message and click Send.
Tips: You do not need to know individual email addresses — the group address handles distribution. For a committee document, give the committee site address, folder and file name; see the SharePoint guide.

How does the email transition work when someone enters or leaves a role? Who handles it?

This is NOT automatic. A human (office staff) must update group memberships and mailbox permissions.

When you are the incoming person (new to a role)

  1. Your committee chair (or the Board, for executive roles) notifies office staff that you are taking over.
  2. Office staff (currently Anna) adds you to the committee mailing list(s) and requests mailbox access from IT.
  3. ITHelp grants you permission to the shared role mailbox.
  4. You can then open the shared mailbox at outlook.office.com and see the full email history.
  5. You begin receiving all committee group emails.

When you are the outgoing person (leaving a role)

  1. Notify your committee chair and office staff of your departure date.
  2. Office staff removes you from the mailing list(s). You stop receiving group emails.
  3. ITHelp removes your mailbox access. You can no longer open it.
  4. The mailbox and all its history remains intact for your successor.

Overlap period

There is no automatic overlap. If you want your successor to start seeing emails before your access is removed, ask office staff to add them early. A brief overlap is good practice.

Who does what

ActionWho handles it
Notify staff of the changeOutgoing or incoming person, or chair
Add / remove people from mailing listsOffice staff (Anna)
Grant / revoke shared mailbox accessITHelp / IT admin
Preserve email history in role mailboxAutomatic — the mailbox retains everything
For the President and executive officers: You do not need to know the technical steps — staff and ITHelp handle them. Your job is to make sure the transition is communicated to office staff promptly.

Staff who need to administer these changes should see the Staff page and the M365 Email Groups & Roles reference.

How do I find phone numbers for Board, committee, and staff members?

There is no centralized online directory with phone numbers in the Microsoft 365 system. Most members do not list personal numbers publicly. Here are your options:

  1. Ask office staff. Email office@sandiahomeowners.org and request the phone number(s) you need. Staff maintain internal contact lists.
  2. Ask your committee chair. Chairs typically maintain a roster with phone numbers shared privately.
  3. Check the SHHA community directory (if available on the SHHA website or as a printed/PDF document).
  4. Board and executive contacts. Board members should receive a contact list at the start of their term. If you have not received one, ask the President or office staff.
For emergencies: Email ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org and office@sandiahomeowners.org simultaneously, mark the subject as URGENT, and explain the situation. Staff can relay messages.
Suggestion for chairs: Maintain a simple phone/email contact sheet for your group and share it privately at the start of each term.

How do I find committee web pages on the SHHA website?

  1. Go to sandiahomeowners.org.
  2. Look for a Committees menu in the top navigation bar or sidebar.
  3. Click through to find the specific committee.
Note: Public committee web pages are informational (schedules, descriptions). Working documents are on SharePoint, not the public website.

Where do I find minutes from committee or Board meetings?

Meeting minutes are typically stored in the committee's SharePoint document library.

  1. Open your committee's SharePoint site (see SharePoint access above).
  2. Click Documents in the left sidebar.
  3. Look for a folder called "Minutes", "Meeting Minutes", or similar. Some committees organize by year (e.g., Documents > 2026 > Minutes).
  4. Click into the folder to see individual files.

If minutes are not in SharePoint: ask your committee chair. Board minutes may also be posted on the SHHA website once approved.

How do I submit an article for The GRIT newsletter?

Use the GRIT content rules and submission guide to choose a contribution type and prepare your files, then submit through the GRIT Submission Portal. That guide maintains the deadline and approved rules.

For editorial questions or help submitting, email griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org. For production work, use the monthly editor procedure.

How do I send an email blast to all SHHA residents?

You cannot send an email blast yourself. Blasts to the full membership are sent by office staff using a bulk email system.

How to request an email blast

  1. Draft your message. Include any links or images.
  2. Email your draft to office@sandiahomeowners.org with a subject like "Email blast request — [topic]."
  3. Specify the audience. All residents? A specific section?
  4. Include your desired send date. Give staff a few business days lead time.
  5. Staff will review and send.

Who has oversight over email blasts?

  • Office staff are the gatekeepers — they control the bulk email system.
  • Board approval may be required for policy statements, financial updates, or messages on behalf of the Board. Ask the President or office manager if unsure.
  • Routine operational messages (meeting reminders, committee announcements) typically do not need separate Board approval.
Important: Do not send mass emails by putting all resident addresses in To or CC. This exposes everyone's email, triggers spam filters, and is not the proper process.

When should I contact IT Help?

Contact ITHelp@sandiahomeowners.org if:

  • You cannot access SharePoint — "Access Denied" or "You need permission" error
  • You are not receiving committee emails
  • You never received or cannot find your Microsoft invitation email
  • You cannot see a shared role inbox after trying the steps above
  • You are unsure which email address to use
  • You are stuck sharing a file
  • You need your invitation resent
  • You see unexpected Microsoft prompts (Teams invitations, license warnings, etc.)
  • You need prior email history retrieved from the archive
  • You need role mailbox access set up or changed
  • You cannot find the SharePoint link for your committee

Contact office staff (office@sandiahomeowners.org) if:

  • You need someone added to or removed from a committee mailing list
  • You need a phone number or contact info for Board / committee / staff
  • You want to submit a GRIT article but don't know the editor's email
  • You want to request an email blast to residents
  • You need to report a leadership transition
Needing help is completely normal. The Microsoft 365 guest system can be confusing. ITHelp and office staff are there to sort it out.

When you email ITHelp, include:

  • Your full name
  • The email address you use for SHHA
  • A screenshot of any error message (if possible)
  • A brief description of what you were trying to do and what happened instead

Where can I find IT systems and access information?

Systems Inventory describes the services SHHA uses. Controls & Security explains safe access and where to get help. IT maintainers should start with IT Infrastructure and Handover and obtain the relevant private operating guides through office staff.

How do I create a form for a survey RSVP or headcount?

For a new SHHA form, start with Google Forms and the forms and results-sharing guide. Google Forms is preferred because Microsoft’s external sharing choices can be awkward. The guide explains the respondent link, the separate read-only results spreadsheet, and the Microsoft Forms alternative. Ask office staff to create or locate the SHHA-owned form.

pages.html:
Send this page to neighbors, committee chairs, Board members, and volunteers who want to contribute to the GRIT.

Note: This is practical writing and photo guidance, not the official publication policy. Read the GRIT content rules and submission guide for the approved section rules and submission process. Approvals and final editorial decisions remain with the Communications & Publications Committee and the current GRIT editor.

Welcome

The GRIT is the community newsletter of Sandia Heights. It is not a newspaper, a social media feed, or an HOA enforcement bulletin.

It is a place for neighbors to share information, ideas, stories, photographs, events, accomplishments, local history, and community knowledge.

The best articles help residents feel more connected to the place they live and the people who live here.

Quick Submission Tips

  • Write for a neighbor holding the printed GRIT in their hands.
  • Make the local connection obvious: why does this matter in Sandia Heights?
  • Send original image files separately instead of embedding them in a Word document.
  • Include captions and names for people in photos when possible.
  • Use a clear title and include dates, locations, and contact information when relevant.
  • Expect light editing for clarity, length, style, and available space.

Know Your Audience

The GRIT is primarily a print publication. Approximately 1,800 printed copies are distributed each month.

A digital version is also emailed and posted online, but only a few hundred readers typically access the issue electronically.

Write for someone holding a printed copy in their hands. If a link or QR code is useful, include it, but do not make the article depend on readers clicking around online.

What Makes Good GRIT Content?

Ask yourself: Why should a Sandia Heights resident care?

Good topics often include:

  • Local wildlife
  • Gardening in Sandia Heights
  • Hiking and trails
  • Neighborhood history
  • Volunteer efforts
  • Community events
  • Local organizations
  • Wildfire preparedness
  • Astronomy and dark skies
  • Interesting neighbors
  • Practical homeowner knowledge
  • Kids' activities
  • Seasonal topics

The strongest articles are relevant to both place, meaning Sandia Heights, and time, meaning what is happening now.

Avoid HOA Nag-Grams

Readers generally do not enjoy being scolded. Instead of "Residents should stop doing X," try "Here is why X matters."

Teach. Explain. Entertain. Tell stories. Share useful information.

A reader who learns something interesting is more likely to change behavior than a reader who feels criticized.

Bring Your Personality

The GRIT does not need to sound like a government report. Humor, storytelling, local anecdotes, and personal experiences are welcome.

Articles can be informative while still being warm, neighborly, and enjoyable to read.

Photographs Matter

The printed GRIT is black and white. An image that looks beautiful in color may become muddy and difficult to understand when printed.

Good Photos

Useful photos usually have:

  • Strong contrast
  • A clear subject
  • Simple composition
  • A large foreground object
  • Distinct separation between subject and background

Photos That Are Hard To Print

Photos often print poorly when they have:

  • Distant subjects
  • Heavy shadows
  • Low contrast
  • Busy backgrounds
  • Lots of similar colors that become the same shade of gray

Image Guidelines

Whenever possible:

  • Submit original image files.
  • Do not embed images inside Word documents.
  • Provide captions.
  • Identify people in photographs.
  • Submit multiple image options.

The editor may crop, resize, or adjust images for publication.

Length

Shorter is usually better.

  • Announcement: 50-150 words
  • Short article: 200-500 words
  • Feature article: 500-1,000 words

If an article is longer, the editor may shorten it for space.

Final Thought

The best GRIT articles answer one question: What would make a neighbor stop flipping pages and read this?

If the article is local, timely, useful, interesting, or amusing, you are probably on the right track.

Internal reference for the Communications & Publications Committee, GRIT editor, layout volunteers, and office staff. This page tracks the working rhythm and handoffs behind each issue.

Editor contact: griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org. Use this address for editorial correspondence. The shhagrit@gmail.com account is only a convenience for Google Drive and file sharing; do not email that Gmail address.

Preparing an issue? Follow the GRIT Monthly Editor Procedure for issue planning, direct Markdown download, the optional Google Docs template, files, and layout handoff. This page covers the production schedule, responsibilities, and approval sequence.

Purpose

The Communications & Publications Committee produces the GRIT, the monthly community newsletter of the Sandia Heights Homeowners Association.

This page is an internal operating reference. It is not the public contributor guide and it is not a replacement for official publication policy.

Audience And Format

  • Primary medium: printed newsletter, approximately 1,800 copies distributed monthly.
  • Secondary medium: digital PDF distributed by email and posted online.
  • Digital reach: email distribution reaches approximately 3,000 subscribers, with typical open/click rates of 200-300 readers per issue.

Because most readers receive the printed edition, publication schedules and content selection should prioritize the print audience.

Monthly Schedule

Before the submission deadline: Content collection

Committee chairs, Board members, residents, and staff submit articles, announcements, photographs, classifieds, and other content.

Submissions should be entered through sandiaheightsgrit.app.

1st of the preceding month: Submission deadline

Submit content by the 1st of the month preceding publication. For example, submissions for the December issue are due November 1. Late submissions may be held for a future issue.

20th-25th: Editorial Review

The Editor:

  • Reviews submissions
  • Performs copy editing
  • Requests revisions if needed
  • Selects photographs and artwork
  • Determines article placement
  • Resolves layout constraints

The Editor may shorten or edit submissions for clarity, space, style, and consistency.

25th-29th: Layout And Proofing

The Editor and layout volunteers:

  • Assemble the issue in Adobe InDesign
  • Verify links, captions, dates, and contact information
  • Prepare advertisements and classifieds
  • Generate proof PDFs

Committee members review the PDF draft and provide comments. In the current Google Drive monthly issue folder under shhagrit@gmail.com, create a Draft review folder, put the draft PDF there, then right-click the folder and choose Share → General access → Anyone with the link → Commenter. Send reviewers the folder link with a comment deadline.

After the comment period, the editor sends required changes to the layout assistant through Upwork. The layout assistant reads the layout package from Google Drive and uploads the revised layout and PDF back there. Check that the edits have been implemented. The layout assistant creates a new final PDF with the edits incorporated; retain the original draft PDF and its comments as a separate file. Follow the draft review and final-PDF sharing steps.

Final Board / Secretary Review And Printer Access

After comments and edits are complete, place the new final PDF in a separate Final folder in the monthly Google Drive issue folder, outside the draft-review folder. Share the PDF itself as Anyone with the link → Viewer. Send the new PDF's view-only link to the Board for an early preview, the printer, the Secretary, and the Office, identifying the current issue/version.

This gives the printer direct access to the final PDF in Google Drive and avoids passing large PDF files around as email attachments. It also lets the printer prepare the proof in parallel while content review is finishing.

The Google Drive link should be treated as the authoritative file for the issue. Avoid sending large PDF attachments unless there is a specific reason.

Proof Approval

The Office reviews and approves the printer proof after the Secretary has approved the issue content.

Normal path:

  1. Editor sends the view-only final-PDF link to the Board for an early preview, the printer, the Secretary, and the Office.
  2. Printer uses the Google Drive PDF to prepare the proof in parallel.
  3. Secretary approves the content.
  4. The Office reviews the printer proof.
  5. The Office approves the proof if it matches the approved content.

If the Secretary requests changes, which should be infrequent:

  1. The Office does not approve the proof.
  2. The editor makes the requested content change.
  3. A new revised final PDF is uploaded to Google Drive and its current view-only link is sent to the Board, printer, Secretary, and the Office.
  4. The printer prepares a revised proof.
  5. The Office reviews and approves only after the corrected content is approved.

Printer Handoff

The printer should have access to the final Google Drive PDF link as early as practical once the issue goes to Board / Secretary review.

Office staff and the editor should confirm:

  • The printer can access the Google Drive file.
  • The printer knows which PDF is the final/current version.
  • The proof is based on the Secretary-approved content.
  • The expected print completion and delivery timing are clear.

Distribution

Office staff:

  • Coordinate printed newsletter distribution.
  • Send email distribution.
  • Post the digital version online.

Long-term source archive

After approval, the editor obtains the complete editable source package from the layout assistant and preserves it in the Office's OneDrive monthly issue folder. Sign in with griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org, the same account used to collect the ads. Keep the InDesign source and linked assets, final edited text, approved PDF, and approved printer proof together for long-term archiving. See the full archive checklist.

Working Roles

  • Communications & Publications Committee: owns the GRIT as a committee function and supports editorial direction.
  • Editor: reviews submissions, edits copy, selects content, resolves fit/placement, sends the final issue for review, and gives the printer direct Google Drive access.
  • Secretary: approves the content before the proof is approved.
  • Printer: uses the Google Drive PDF to prepare the proof in parallel with final content review.
  • Office: reviews and approves the printer proof after Secretary approval, coordinates print/distribution handoff, and holds approval if content changes are requested.
  • Layout volunteers: assemble the issue in InDesign and prepare proof PDFs as needed.

Internal Checkpoints

  • Are events still timely by the time the printed GRIT reaches residents?
  • Are dates, locations, names, contact details, and URLs checked?
  • Are photos likely to work in black-and-white print?
  • Are ads and classifieds in the correct issue folder?
  • Is the final Google Drive PDF link clearly identified as the authoritative version?
  • Has the printer been copied or otherwise given direct access to the Google Drive PDF?
  • Has the Secretary approved the content?
  • Is the Office approving the proof only after content approval?
  • If changes are requested, has proof approval been held until the revised content is ready?

Goal

The purpose of the schedule is to ensure that:

  • Events are announced before they occur.
  • Information remains timely and useful.
  • Print readers receive current content.
  • Workload is distributed among volunteers and staff.
  • Publication is not dependent on any one individual.
  • The printer can work from the current Google Drive file instead of oversized email attachments.

Use this page each month when preparing the GRIT issue layout.

Start with the editorial package. The GRIT Monthly Editor Procedure explains how to prepare the text, ads, and images for layout. Use the steps below when you are doing the InDesign layout yourself.

Monthly Steps

  • Copy the template into the month folder.
  • Rename the file for the current month.

Monthly Settings

Change monthly accent color

  • In InDesign: Window → Color → Swatches
  • Select Issue Accent Color.
  • Enter RGB value, or use the eyedropper tool.

Folder Structure

Your local folder structure should look like this:

month_name
  - Ads
  - Images

Download Assets

Ads

Download the prepared ads from the current issue's Ads folder in Google Drive. The editor collects the Office's OneDrive ads and copies them into this layout package.

Images

Download the matching Images folder from the Google Drive issue package. The editor gathers the actual files from the submissions app and email; filenames must match the text references.

Skeleton and Layout Setup

Ensure all guides are visible

  • View → Grids & Guides → Show Guides
  • View → Screen Mode → Normal

Insert pages

Insert enough pages so the issue ends on a multiple of 4.

Insert ads and images

  • Use ads in planned ad frames.
  • Use Cmd+Shift+Click to turn a master frame into an editable box.
  • Use Cmd+D to place the image.

Image fitting behavior

The image masters are created with an Object Style that fits the image you place into the largest dimension.

Preserve the editable layout package

Upload the editable InDesign source and all linked assets back to the Google Drive issue folder, along with the PDFs. After final proof approval, supply the editor with the complete source package for long-term archiving in OneDrive. Preserve the folder structure and filenames; a PDF alone does not contain the editable layout source.

GRIT Layout FAQ

Do I need to use exact folder names?

Yes. Keep the month folder with Ads and Images subfolders so links and placement are predictable.

Why does Cmd+Shift+Click matter?

It unlocks master-page frames so you can edit a specific issue page without changing the master itself.

What if page count is not a multiple of 4?

Insert pages until the total is divisible by 4. Print layout and booklet flow depend on this.

  • GRIT Internal Production Reference
  • Quick Reference

For residents, neighbors, Board and committee members, office staff, and anyone contributing to the GRIT. Start by choosing the section that fits your contribution, then submit it through the GRIT Submission Portal.

Approved rules, in a reader-friendly format. This page presents the GRIT Content Rules & Submission Guide approved by the Communications & Publications Committee on June 22, 2026. The original approved PDF is available for reference.

Start here

  1. Choose your section. Use the guide below to decide whether your submission is a community contribution, classified, local event, or advertisement.
  2. Prepare your content. Check the rules for that section. For photos and graphics, check that details remain clear in black and white.
  3. Submit through the portal. Open the GRIT Submission Portal and select the category that best matches your content. If you are unsure, choose the closest match; editors can reassign it.

Need help or unable to use the portal? Email your submission or questions to the GRIT editor at griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org.

Plan for the next issue. The GRIT submission deadline is the 1st of the month preceding publication. For example, submissions for the December issue are due November 1. Submit through the GRIT Submission Portal. Publication in a particular issue is not guaranteed.

Keep it informative, constructive, and neighborly

The GRIT welcomes content that educates, celebrates community involvement, shares useful information, and helps residents connect with one another.

Articles work best when they explain an issue, provide context, share an experience, or offer a solution. Content focused mainly on criticism, complaints, or repeated reminders is less likely to be effective. Editors may edit it for tone and clarity, or it may fail editorial review.

Choose your section

Section Use it for Key point
Community Contributions Stories, opinions, experiences, and useful community information. Write in a personal capacity, rather than on behalf of SHHA or a committee.
Classifieds Brief personal or small-business announcements. Maximum 300 characters; plain text only.
Local Events Community activities and public-interest events. Include date, time, and location when applicable. No commercial promotion.
Advertising Promotional or marketing content. Contact the SHHA office about paid advertising.

Community Contributions

This is the main section for resident-submitted content. Most submissions received through the portal are considered for this section unless another section is more appropriate.

Residents, Board members, committee members, office staff, and other community contributors may submit here when writing in a personal capacity, rather than on behalf of SHHA or an SHHA committee.

Examples include:

  • Opinions and commentary.
  • Educational content and personal experiences relevant to the community.
  • Local history, nature, and wildlife observations.
  • Neighbor appreciation and community announcements.
  • Other topics likely to interest Sandia Heights residents.

Whose views are these? Community Contributions reflect the author's views. They do not necessarily represent SHHA, its Board of Directors, committees, employees, or volunteers.

Classifieds

Classifieds give residents and local businesses a simple, equitable way to share brief announcements. Examples include services offered, items for sale, lost and found, requests for assistance, lessons or tutoring, pet sitting, babysitting, handyman services, and similar personal or small-business notices.

Requirement What to do
Length Keep your listing to a maximum of 300 characters.
Format Use plain text only: no images, logos, flyers, or special formatting.
Contact details You may include contact information and website links. Editors may shorten long web addresses or turn them into QR codes (scannable squares that open a link).
Eligibility Open to residents and businesses with a physical presence in the Sandia Heights area.
Repeat listings Resubmit each month if you want continued publication. Business-related listings are limited to one publication per calendar quarter to encourage variety and reduce repetitive content.
Publication Subject to available space and editorial discretion.

A submission is not a standing order. Classifieds must be resubmitted for each month in which publication is desired. For business-related listings, the once-per-calendar-quarter limit still applies.

Local Events

Use this section for upcoming community activities and public-interest events, such as gatherings, educational programs, workshops, performances, fundraisers, meetups, and similar public events.

  • Who can submit: residents and organizations with a physical presence in the Sandia Heights area, or events taking place within Sandia Heights that interest the Sandia Heights community.
  • Include the essentials: date, time, and location when applicable.
  • Submit again for another month: listings must be resubmitted each month if continued publication is desired.

Recurring events are not automatically republished. Commercial advertising, promotional content, and business marketing disguised as event listings are not permitted in Local Events.

Advertising

Any submission that includes images, logos, extended promotional text, or marketing-style content may be treated as paid advertising.

For advertising inquiries, contact the SHHA office at office@sandiahomeowners.org.

Choose photos and graphics that work in print

Photos and graphics are encouraged and can bring a story to life. The GRIT appears in color online and is mailed in black and white to more than 1,800 Sandia Heights households each month.

  1. Choose high-resolution images. Use images with enough detail to look clear when printed.
  2. Check important details in black and white. Make sure readers can still see the subject, labels, and other information.
  3. Use enough contrast. Text and important details should stand out from the background.
  4. Do not rely on color alone. A label or highlight that works in color may disappear when printed.

Example from the approved guide: the yellow callout works in color but is hard to see in black and white. A different color choice for the callout box and text can make the printed version readable.

For more practical writing and photo advice, see the GRIT Contributor Guide.

Send your submission

  1. Open the GRIT Submission Portal. This is the preferred submission route. It helps editors track content, communicate with contributors, manage revisions, and route submissions to the right section.
  2. Select the best-fitting category and submit your content. If you are unsure, choose the closest category; editors may move your submission to a more appropriate section.
  3. If you cannot use the portal, email the editor. Send your submission to griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org.

What happens after you submit?

  • Editorial review: editors may edit for clarity, length, style, formatting, and available space. Their goal is to preserve your voice and intent.
  • Substantive changes: if significant changes are proposed, editors will make a good-faith effort to provide the revised version for your review and approval.
  • Minor changes: grammar, style, formatting, and changes for space constraints may be made without additional review.
  • Issue placement: publication in a particular issue cannot be guaranteed. Depending on space, timing, and editorial needs, content may appear in a future issue, be abbreviated, or occasionally be declined.

For complete details about publication, editing, and contributor rights, read the GRIT Submission Terms & Conditions (PDF).

Ready to contribute?

Submit through the GRIT portal, or ask the GRIT editor for help. For policy questions, contact the Communications & Publications Committee.

pages.html:
For the GRIT editor and anyone covering the role. Start by selecting the correct issue in the submissions app, then follow the steps below through layout, approval, and archiving.

Editor contact: griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org. This address also signs in to the office's OneDrive for collecting ads and archiving the finished layout package. The Google account shhagrit@gmail.com is for Google Drive/file-sharing convenience only; do not email that Gmail address.

The route from content to archive

Google Drive is the working issue folder; OneDrive is the long-term archive. Ads, text, and images come together in Google Drive. The layout assistant reads that package and uploads the layout and PDF there. After approval, preserve the complete source package in OneDrive.

Open the flowchart at full size.

1. Open the workspaces and issue folder

  1. Confirm access to the submissions app's editor area, Google Drive under shhagrit@gmail.com, the office's OneDrive using griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org, and the existing layout contract in Upwork → Messages. Ask the Office to arrange missing access.
  2. In Google Drive, open My Drive → Monthly Issues → [year] → [issue folder]. Create the issue folder if needed, including Ads and Images subfolders. Clearly name combined issues.
  3. Keep this issue's text, assets, layout files, and PDF versions together. Google Drive and OneDrive are separate services; copying between them is a manual step.

For sign-in help, use Quick Links & Directory. Keep passwords and account-recovery details out of issue documents.

2. Plan the issue

  1. In the app's Issue Planning area, check the selected month, especially when finishing an earlier or combined issue.
  2. Review new submissions and the backlog. Use Plan to select items, then Content Flow to arrange the reading order.
  3. Check dates, titles, bylines, relevance, and space. Follow up on expected material and resolve placeholders before layout. A contributor's private contact details are not automatically a published byline.
  4. Agree the word/page budget and turnaround with the layout assistant. The final printed booklet must have a page count divisible by four. Follow the approved content and editing rules when shortening or revising contributions.

The GRIT submission deadline is the 1st of the month preceding publication. For example, submissions for the December issue are due November 1. Confirm layout and proofing dates with the Office and layout assistant; see the production schedule and responsibilities.

3. Collect ads and images

  1. Sign in to the office's OneDrive with griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org. Office staff supply current ads by the issue deadline. Use GRIT Editor Workspace → Monthly Issues → [year] → [issue] → Ads, or the workspace the Office provides.
  2. Download the current ads, extract the ZIP if necessary, and upload the actual files to the Google Drive issue's Ads folder.
  3. Collect photographs and graphics from the submissions app and email, then upload them to Images. Copy carried-over or reusable artwork into this issue without disturbing earlier archives or master files.

Text references do not contain image files. Supply the actual images, with filenames and captions that match the text. Check that important details remain readable in black and white.

4. Download the issue's Markdown

Markdown is plain text with formatting markers, such as # before a heading. A .md file gives the layout assistant the issue text and image-filename notes.

  1. In the submissions app, open Newsletter Preview and confirm the issue month and reading order.
  2. Choose Download Markdown to download all the planned issue's Markdown in one file. It normally appears in your computer's Downloads folder.

The Google Docs/Markdown-sidebar workflow is optional. You can use the app's direct download without going through Google Docs.

Optional: edit in the Google Docs template

  1. If you prefer editing in Google Docs, copy Master Template Content Editing into the issue folder. Paste the issue's Markdown into GRIT → Open Markdown Sidebar and choose Insert at cursor. Work in the copy.
  2. Keep titles as Heading 1, bylines as Heading 2, and body text as ordinary paragraphs. Ask the template maintainer about unfamiliar authorization prompts.
  3. Export the edited document to Markdown using the approved template method. Compare the result with the document: the sidebar's download may contain its earlier input rather than later document edits. Resolve any mismatch before layout.

5. Review the text and image notes

  1. Read the issue from start to finish. Correct spelling, dates, links, titles, and bylines; remove placeholders and replace any “Untitled submission” headings.
  2. Identify each intended image by its exact filename, caption, and any placement note; for example, [PHOTO: fence-illustration.png]. Confirm the file is in Images. Update the text reference if you rename a file.
  3. Follow the contributor-review requirements for substantive edits. Recheck any illustration for accuracy and print readability.

6. Upload the checked text to Google Drive

  1. Open the final .md file in a plain-text editor. Check the article order, recent corrections, titles, bylines, and image filenames.
  2. In the Google Drive issue folder, choose New → File upload. Give the text file a clear issue/version name and identify the current version.

7. Hand the package to the layout assistant

The package is ready when the checked text, current ads, and all referenced images are present and open correctly.

  1. Use the existing Upwork → Messages conversation. Send the Google Drive issue-folder link, exact text filename/version, placement notes, outstanding items, and the agreed first-PDF deadline.
  2. Confirm the layout assistant can open the folder. The assistant reads the package from Google Drive and uploads the editable layout files and draft PDF back there.
  3. Coordinate later corrections through the same conversation, identifying exactly what changed.

8. Review the PDF and complete approval

Share the draft for comments

  1. Check the returned PDF against the text and assets: article completeness, bylines, dates, links, captions, images, ads, and black-and-white readability.
  2. Create Draft review inside the monthly Google Drive folder and put the draft PDF there. Keep working documents and source assets in the other issue folders.
  3. Right-click Draft review → Share → General access → Anyone with the link → Commenter. Choose Copy link, then Done. Send reviewers the folder link, current PDF filename, and a comment deadline with date, time, and time zone.
  4. Review the comments and send agreed corrections to the layout assistant through Upwork. Check that the revised layout incorporates them.

Share the new final PDF as view only

The final version is a new PDF with the edits incorporated. Keep the original commented draft as a separate file.

  1. Have the layout assistant upload the new final PDF to a Final folder alongside Draft review.
  2. Right-click the new PDF itself → Share → General access → Anyone with the link → Viewer. Choose Copy link, then Done. Check that the link opens in a private browser window.
  3. Send that PDF link to the Board for an early preview, the printer, the Secretary, and the Office. Identify the issue/version and response deadline.

Approve the content and printer proof

  1. Obtain the Secretary's content approval. The printer can prepare a proof in parallel from the linked PDF.
  2. The Office approves the final printer proof after Secretary content approval, checking that it matches the approved PDF.
  3. If changes are required, hold proof approval. Have the layout assistant upload a new revised PDF, send its view-only link to the same recipients, and repeat content approval and printer-proof approval.
  4. Coordinate print distribution, email distribution, and online posting with the Office.

9. Archive the full source package in OneDrive

  1. Ask the layout assistant for the complete editable layout package, including the InDesign source files and all linked images, artwork, and ads. Include any supplied templates and an IDML exchange-format copy if available, so a future layout assistant can reopen the issue.
  2. Add the final edited text/Markdown, any Google Docs editing export used, the approved PDF, and the approved printer proof. Preserve the folder structure and filenames used by the layout.
  3. Sign in to OneDrive using griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org. Open the Office's GRIT Editor Workspace → Monthly Issues → [year] → [issue], or the archive location confirmed by the Office, and upload the full package.
  4. Open the archived source files, linked assets, and PDFs to confirm the upload is complete. Clearly identify the approved version and any combined issue.

Keep completed issue folders for long-term archiving. Preserve earlier issues and the complete source package, so future editors can reuse or rebuild an issue. Google Drive's working folder does not automatically synchronize to OneDrive.

If something is missing or looks wrong

What you see What to check next
The planned articles seem to have disappeared. Check the selected issue month; the default may have advanced.
A downloaded Markdown file is missing from Google Drive. Look in your computer's Downloads folder, verify the file, then upload it to the issue folder.
A recent Google Docs correction is missing from the Markdown. Compare the export with the document and ask the template maintainer to resolve the export method before layout.
The assistant cannot find an image. Check that the actual file is uploaded and that its filename exactly matches the text reference.
The GRIT menu does not appear. Wait for the copied template to load, then confirm you copied the script-enabled Master Template Content Editing document. Ask the maintainer if it still does not appear.
Sign-in, authorization, or file sharing fails. Confirm the intended GRIT account and ask the office/current editor or IT help to check access. Do not change organization security settings to get around the prompt.

For Google Drive sharing and inherited access, use Google's guide. For hands-on layout work, see the GRIT Layout Monthly Guide; for schedules and roles, see the GRIT Internal Production Reference.

Operational reference for office staff, IT admin, and future volunteers — mailing lists, shared mailboxes, licensing, SOPs, and governance.

Any SHHA volunteer who wants their own SHHA email address may have one. A personal address such as first.last@sandiahomeowners.org is available to volunteers as well as staff. Volunteers may also keep using personal email for committee messages and approved SharePoint guest access. Ask office staff for your preferred option; see account setup and current license costs.

For an email-address request, contact office staff. For setup or access problems, contact IT Help.

Quick Overview

SHHA uses two different patterns for email collaboration:

PatternTechnologyExamples
Committee mailing lists Microsoft Groups shha-all@, csc@, acc@
Role-based addresses Shared mailboxes president@, cscchair@, accchair@

Design Principles

  • Role continuity over individual ownership — email addresses stay constant when people rotate in/out.
  • Least cost for volunteers — external volunteers do not require paid M365 licenses.
  • Membership awareness — Toolbox’s Automatic emailer reports detected changes according to timing and delivery settings; verify membership in Microsoft 365.
  • Institutional archive — admin@ is included in all groups as a permanent archive recipient.

Microsoft Groups (Mailing Lists)

Each committee has a Microsoft Group that acts as its mailing list.

GroupAddress
All membersshha-all@sandiahomeowners.org
CSCcsc@sandiahomeowners.org
ACCacc@sandiahomeowners.org
OthersOne group per committee

Behavior: Sending to the group distributes to all members. Membership is maintained by staff (primary owner: Anna). External participants can be included.

Shared Mailboxes (Role Inboxes)

Only six officer role addresses are shared mailboxes tied to positions, not people: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, and CSC Chair. Other committee chairs and task-force leads use their own account and the committee mailing list.

RoleAddress
CSC Chaircscchair@sandiahomeowners.org
ACC Chairaccchair@sandiahomeowners.org
Presidentpresident@sandiahomeowners.org
Vice Presidentvicepresident@sandiahomeowners.org
Secretarysecretary@sandiahomeowners.org
Treasurertreasurer@sandiahomeowners.org

Each incoming officer receives both Full Access and Send As permission through the officer's own licensed SHHA account. Officers cannot log in directly to the shared mailbox and must add it manually in Outlook because it may not appear automatically. For official role correspondence, send from the role mailbox or copy it so the shared mailbox remains the archive.

Access model

  • People do not log in directly as the role mailbox.
  • Authorized users open the shared mailbox from their own licensed account.
  • Example: phil.krehbiel@sandiahomeowners.org can open accchair@sandiahomeowners.org.

When leadership changes

  1. Remove predecessor access.
  2. Grant successor access.
  3. Keep the role mailbox address unchanged.

Archive Mailbox (admin@)

  • admin@ is a member of all groups.
  • Purpose: permanent archive and continuity.
  • admin@ is not actively monitored for normal operations.

Toolbox Automatic emailer notifications

SHHA Toolbox’s Automatic emailer observes Microsoft 365 groups automatically. A first successful read establishes a baseline without an introductory email. Mailing-list timing can be Instant, Daily digest or Off. Confirm membership in Microsoft 365; a missing notification does not prove a membership edit failed. Review Recent emails and service status for delivery questions.

  • Provides audit visibility.
  • Alerts staff to unexpected changes.
  • Supports handoffs and troubleshooting.

Licensing and External Volunteers

User typeLicense needed?Capabilities
External volunteersNoGroup email delivery, SharePoint guest access
Licensed volunteer, officer or staff memberYes (paid M365)Own SHHA mailbox; approved shared-mailbox access where applicable. Administrator rights require separate authorization.

Responsibilities Matrix

ResponsibilityPrimaryBackupNotes
Maintain committee group membershipAnna (staff)IT adminAdd/remove members, verify accuracy
Manage shared mailbox permissionsAnna + IT adminIT adminRemove predecessor, add successor
Ensure admin@ in all groupsIT adminAnnaRequired for archive continuity
Monitor membership-change notificationsAnnaIT adminReview Automatic emailer status and Recent emails
Troubleshoot delivery/access issuesIT adminAnnaIncludes mailbox permissions and group settings

SOP: Add a Person to a Committee Mailing List

  1. Confirm committee and target group address.
  2. Ask whether the person wants their own SHHA mailbox or will use personal email as an invited guest.
  3. Add to the correct Microsoft Group membership.
  4. Confirm admin@ remains a member.
  5. Confirm membership directly in Microsoft 365. Review Automatic emailer timing and Recent emails; Off or Daily timing can explain why an immediate notice did not arrive.
  6. Ask the group owner or new member to test delivery, or send a test message yourself.

SOP: Remove a Person from a Committee Mailing List

  1. Confirm removal request and effective date.
  2. Remove member from the Microsoft Group.
  3. Confirm the removal directly in Microsoft 365; review Automatic emailer timing and Recent emails when checking delivery.
  4. If person held one of the six officer roles, check related shared mailbox permissions.

SOP: Leadership Transition for Role Inbox

  1. Identify affected role mailbox (e.g., accchair@).
  2. Remove outgoing person's mailbox permissions.
  3. Grant incoming person's mailbox permissions.
  4. Validate that incoming person can open the shared mailbox from their own account.
  5. Keep address and historical content in place for continuity.

SOP: New Committee Creation

  1. Create new Microsoft Group for the committee.
  2. Add initial committee members.
  3. Add admin@ as member for archiving.
  4. Ensure membership-change notifications are active.
  5. Record the group in the committee/group inventory.

Governance Rules

  • Every committee must have exactly one official mailing-list group.
  • Every committee group must include admin@.
  • Shared mailbox addresses represent roles and must not be treated as personal identities.
  • Access to shared role inboxes must be updated promptly on leadership change.
  • Membership changes should be performed by staff owner (Anna) or IT admin only.

Recommended Recordkeeping

Maintain a simple inventory table (in the wiki or internal operations file) with:

  • Committee name
  • Group email address
  • Current chair role mailbox (if applicable)
  • Current permission holders
  • Last membership review date
  • Last updated by
This makes volunteer/staff handoff much easier.

Common Issues and Checks

Person does not receive committee emails

  • Member exists in correct Microsoft Group
  • Email address is correct
  • Sender used the correct group address
  • Recent change triggered notification (confirms update happened)

New officer cannot open role mailbox

  • Shared mailbox permission was granted to the person's licensed account
  • User is opening mailbox from their own account context
  • Predecessor access was removed (to avoid confusion)

Missing archive history

  • admin@ is still a member of the affected group
  • Group delivery settings have not been altered

Handoff Checklist (Staff / Volunteer Transition)

  • Review all committee group memberships for accuracy.
  • Verify all six active officer roles have correct shared mailbox access.
  • Remove stale permissions from former role holders.
  • Confirm admin@ is in every group.
  • Confirm membership-change notification flow is working.
  • Update inventory table and date-stamp the review.

Key Contacts and Ownership

RoleContact
Group membership ownerAnna (staff)
Technical ownerIT admin
Archive mailboxadmin@ (not actively monitored)
If ownership changes, update this section immediately.

Related Resources

  • M365 Email Building Blocks — understand the four email patterns (personal mailbox, shared mailbox, mailing list, alias) and when to use each
  • SOP: New Users, Mailboxes & Groups — step-by-step admin procedures for creating users, shared mailboxes, groups, and aliases
  • Office Onboarding Email Templates — copy-and-send messages for the people who receive new access

pages.html:
SHHA uses four distinct patterns for email addresses in Microsoft 365. Before requesting any new address, understand which pattern fits your need. This page is the reference for anyone planning new committees, roles, or special-purpose addresses.

Shared-mailbox licensing details: Microsoft shared mailbox guidance.

Any SHHA volunteer who wants their own SHHA email address may have one. A personal address such as first.last@sandiahomeowners.org is available to volunteers as well as staff. Volunteers may also keep using personal email for committee messages and approved SharePoint guest access. Ask office staff for your preferred option; see account setup and current license costs.

For an email-address request, contact office staff. For setup or access problems, contact IT Help.

The Four Patterns at a Glance

PatternWhat it isExampleWhen to use it
Personal mailbox; first.last@sandiahomeowners.org A licensed M365 account owned by one person. Has its own login, calendar, OneDrive, etc. anna.smith@sandiahomeowners.org Any volunteer who requests an SHHA email address, plus staff needing an account. Requires a paid license; an email account does not grant administrator rights.
Shared mailbox; role@sandiahomeowners.org A mailbox tied to a position, not a person. Multiple licensed users can open it from their own account. Retains full email history across holders. president@sandiahomeowners.org; cscchair@sandiahomeowners.org Only one of SHHA's six officer roles: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, or CSC Chair. Each officer receives Full Access and Send As through the officer's own licensed account.
Mailing list (Microsoft Group); committee@sandiahomeowners.org A Microsoft 365 group with a committee email address and connected collaboration resources. Configured inbox delivery sends copies to members, including invited guests. It is different from an Exchange distribution list. csc@sandiahomeowners.org; shha-all@sandiahomeowners.org Any group of people who need to receive the same email. Most committees have one. No license cost for external members.
Alias; (additional address on an existing mailbox or group) An extra email address that delivers to an existing mailbox or group. Not a separate mailbox — just an alternative address for the same destination. wildfire@sandiahomeowners.org → delivers to the ESC group or a specific shared mailbox One-off or special-purpose addresses (task forces, events, topical inboxes) where you do not need a separate mailbox with its own history. Use when you want a memorable address that maps to something that already exists.

Which Pattern Do I Need?

Walk through these questions when planning a new email address:

  1. Does a volunteer or staff member want their own SHHA email mailbox?
    • Yes → Personal mailbox (requires a license; talk to IT admin)
    • No → continue
  2. Is this one of the six designated officer role inboxes that must survive personnel changes?
    • Yes → Shared mailbox
    • No → continue
  3. Does the address need to deliver to a group of people?
    • Yes → Mailing list (Microsoft Group)
    • No → continue
  4. Do you just need a convenient address that routes to an existing mailbox or group?
    • Yes → Alias on the appropriate existing mailbox or group
    • No → talk to IT admin to figure out the right approach

Combining Patterns

For a committee or task force, the normal setup is:

WhatPatternTypical result
Committee mailing listMicrosoft GroupOne address that reaches all current members, including external volunteers
Committee documentsSharePoint siteOne group-owned Documents library for the committee record
Friendly alias (optional)Alias on the groupAn additional memorable address that routes to the group
Officer role inbox (only when applicable)Shared mailboxOne of the six officer addresses; never a general chair or task-force mailbox

You generally do not need to create personal mailboxes for volunteers. External volunteers receive group email at their personal addresses (Gmail, Yahoo, etc.) and use SharePoint in a browser.

Archive Rule

Every mailing list (Microsoft Group) must include admin@sandiahomeowners.org as a member. This is the archive account that preserves all committee email for continuity and records. It is not monitored for support.

Cost Summary

PatternLicense cost
Personal mailboxRequires a paid M365 license
Shared mailboxUsually no separate mailbox license up to 50 GB. Delegates need licensed Exchange Online mailboxes; archiving, hold and advanced features can require additional licenses.
Mailing list (Group)Free
AliasFree (added to an existing mailbox or group)

Where to Go Next

  • Need to create a new user or shared mailbox? See SOP: New Users, Mailboxes & Groups.
  • Need to tell someone what to do next? Use Office Onboarding Email Templates.
  • Need to add/remove members from an existing group? See the SOPs in M365 Email Groups, Role Inboxes & Responsibilities.
  • Not sure what you need? Email ithelp@sandiahomeowners.org with a description of the goal and IT admin will recommend the right pattern.

pages.html:
This SOP is written for SHHA staff who are comfortable with basic Microsoft admin work and need a reliable step-by-step process for setting up new groups, shared mailboxes, and related addresses.

Any SHHA volunteer who wants their own SHHA email address may have one. A personal address such as first.last@sandiahomeowners.org is available to volunteers as well as staff. Volunteers may also keep using personal email for committee messages and approved SharePoint guest access. Ask office staff for your preferred option; see account setup and current license costs.

License cost: SHHA currently pays about $7 per month for each licensed account (November 17, 2026). Set up accounts for actual requests; do not buy extra licenses in anticipation of future volunteers. Check whether a suitable paid license is already available before arranging another purchase.

For an email-address request, contact office staff. For setup or access problems, contact IT Help.

Start here every time: admin.microsoft.com

Quick Start: What Are You Trying to Set Up?

If you need... Go to this section
A new task-force or committee mailing address that sends to all members SOP A: Create a Microsoft 365 Group (Mailing List)
A SharePoint document site for a new committee or task force SOP: Create a Committee SharePoint Site
A shared mailbox for one of the six officer roles SOP B: Create a Shared Mailbox
A friendly one-off address like wildfire@sandiahomeowners.org SOP C: Add an Alias
A personal SHHA email account for a volunteer or staff member, such as first.last@sandiahomeowners.org SOP D: Add a Licensed User
An external volunteer using Gmail/Yahoo/etc. SOP E: Add an External Guest

Task Force Fast Path (Most Common New Setup)

For a new short-term task force, the normal pattern is:

  1. Create a Microsoft 365 Group for the task-force mailing list.
  2. Add members (including external guests) and always include admin@sandiahomeowners.org.
  3. If the request is for one of the six officer roles, use SOP B for the role mailbox. Ordinary committee chairs and task-force leads do not get shared mailboxes.
  4. Add an optional Alias (for example, wildfire@sandiahomeowners.org) if a friendlier address is useful.
  5. Confirm the Microsoft 365 group-connected SharePoint site exists; do not create a duplicate.
  6. Configure document permissions using SOP: Create a Committee SharePoint Site and send members the Committee SharePoint Guide.
  7. Test email delivery, update the Quick Links directory, and send the New Committee Or Task Force email if this is a new group.

If you only need one address that emails the whole task force, do SOP A only.

SOP A: Create a Microsoft 365 Group (Mailing List)

Use this for: any committee/task-force address that should email all members.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Teams & groups → Active teams & groups → Add a group

Step-by-step

  1. Open admin.microsoft.com and sign in.
  2. In the left menu, click Teams & groups.
  3. Click Active teams & groups.
  4. Click Add a group.
  5. Select Microsoft 365 as the group type, then click Next.
  6. Enter:
    • Name: Full task-force name (example: Wildfire Preparedness Task Force)
    • Description: Short purpose statement
    Click Next.
  7. Add at least one Owner (usually office staff), then click Next.
  8. Set:
    • Group email address (example: wildfiretf → wildfiretf@sandiahomeowners.org)
    • Privacy: usually Private
    • Leave "Create a team for this group" off unless Teams is explicitly needed
    Click Next then Create group.
  9. After the group is created, open the new group and go to its Settings pane.
  10. Required: check Let people outside the organization email this team.
  11. Required: check Send copies of team emails and events to team members' inboxes.
  12. Go to Members → Add members.
  13. Add all task-force members (internal and external as available).
  14. Required: Add admin@sandiahomeowners.org as a member for archive continuity.
  15. Send a test email to the new group address and confirm delivery.
  16. Send the New Committee Or Task Force email after the group, membership, and any SharePoint site are tested.

Test after every change: whenever membership or a group setting changes, test the group again. You can add yourself temporarily, send a test message, and remove yourself afterward. If external delivery matters, you can also add a personal Gmail account temporarily, test it, and remove it when finished.

Done checklist

  • Group exists
  • Owners added
  • All members added
  • External email enabled
  • Inbox delivery enabled
  • admin@ added
  • Test email delivered after setup and after any later change

SOP B: Create a Shared Mailbox (Six Officer Roles Only)

Use this only for: President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, ACC Chair, or CSC Chair. Shared mailboxes are a little fussy to administer, but officer history is important enough that SHHA keeps it this way.

Do not use this for: ordinary committee chairs, task-force leads, external volunteers, or general committee communication. Use the person's own account and the committee Microsoft Group instead.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Teams & groups → Shared mailboxes → Add a shared mailbox

Step-by-step

  1. Confirm the role is one of the six officer roles above. If it is any other chair or lead, stop and use the committee mailing-list procedure.
  2. Click Add a shared mailbox.
  3. Enter the role name and address, such as president@sandiahomeowners.org.
  4. Save the mailbox, then open its details and choose Members → Edit → Add members.
  5. Add the incoming officer's licensed @sandiahomeowners.org account.
  6. Grant that account both Full Access and Send As. These are separate permissions; grant both.
  7. Send the Officer Shared Mailbox Access email with the direct role address and the wiki link.
  8. Ask the officer to sign in to Outlook with their own account and manually add the shared mailbox. It will not appear automatically in every Outlook setup.
  9. Test that the officer can open the mailbox, read an incoming test message, and send with the role address in the From field.
  10. Tell the officer to send official role correspondence from the role mailbox or copy it. The shared mailbox is the role's archive; a personal inbox is not.

Important notes

  • The officer does not log in directly to the shared mailbox. There is no separate shared-mailbox password to give them.
  • For current Outlook instructions, see Open and use a shared mailbox in Outlook.
  • For a change of officer, remove the outgoing officer's permissions, grant the incoming officer both permissions, and test again.

SOP C: Add an Alias (One-Off Friendly Address)

Use this for: addresses like wildfire@sandiahomeowners.org that should route to an existing group or mailbox.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → select target group/mailbox → Email aliases / Email address settings

Step-by-step

  1. Decide destination first: should alias route to the group or the shared mailbox?
  2. For group destination:
    • Go to Teams & groups → Active teams & groups.
    • Select the group.
    • Open email settings and add alias address.
  3. For shared mailbox destination:
    • Go to Teams & groups → Shared mailboxes.
    • Select mailbox.
    • Open email settings and add alias address.
  4. Save changes.
  5. Send test email to alias and verify it arrives in the expected destination.

SOP D: Add a licensed user for a volunteer or staff member

Use this for: any volunteer requesting an SHHA email address, and staff who need a personal SHHA account (first.last@sandiahomeowners.org).

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Users → Active users → Add a user

Step-by-step

  1. Confirm the person wants their own SHHA email address. Volunteers are eligible; being staff or an officer is not a requirement.
  2. Check existing users for an account belonging to this person, then check whether a suitable paid license is already available. Ask the authorized license purchaser to arrange a license only if this request needs one. Do not purchase spare licenses.
  3. Go to Users → Active users → Add a user. Enter the person's name and first.last@sandiahomeowners.org username.
  4. Generate a temporary password and require a password change at first sign-in. Provide the temporary password through a separate approved channel from the username and welcome instructions.
  5. Assign the appropriate license and finish creating the user. Ordinary email users do not need an administrator role.
  6. Add the account to the approved committee groups. Grant shared-mailbox permissions only when the person holds one of the six designated officer roles.
  7. Have the person sign in to Outlook, receive and send a test message, and open their committee Documents library. Verify the intended account is in use.
  8. Send the licensed-user welcome message from the Office Onboarding Email Templates and link the Volunteer with SHHA Email guide.

SOP E: Add an External Guest (Volunteer)

Use this for: volunteers who choose to keep using personal email; approved guest access avoids an SHHA mailbox license cost.

Menu path: admin.microsoft.com → Users → Guest users (or Entra invite flow)

Step-by-step

  1. Invite external user with personal email address.
  2. Ask them to accept Microsoft invitation email.
  3. After acceptance, add them to needed Microsoft Groups.
  4. Verify they receive a test group email and can open the committee SharePoint Documents library using the invited account.

Audience: SHHA office staff and IT administrators. This is not a committee-member task.

Goal: connect an existing committee Microsoft 365 group to its group-owned SharePoint document library, keep site-page administration with office staff, and give committee members read/write access to documents.

Before You Start

Write down these values before opening Microsoft 365:

Committee nameThe full display name
Microsoft 365 groupThe existing group/mailing-list name
Group emailThe committee mailing-list address
Expected site addresshttps://shha.sharepoint.com/sites/[GROUP-NAME]
Office ownersPrimary and backup office/admin accounts

The finished site should be Private. Office staff are Owners / Full Control. Committee members have Contribute access to documents and do not administer the home page.

Step 1: Find The Existing Group-Connected Site

A Microsoft 365 group normally provisions a connected SharePoint team site. If the mailing list already exists, do not begin by creating another site or group.

  1. Try https://shha.sharepoint.com/sites/[GROUP-NAME].
  2. If that does not open, go to admin.microsoft.com → Show all → Admin centers → SharePoint.
  3. Open Sites → Active sites.
  4. Search for both the committee's full name and group name.
  5. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, open Teams & groups → Active teams & groups, select the group, and confirm its type is Microsoft 365.

If the group-connected site appears in Active sites, open it and continue.

If the Microsoft 365 group exists but no connected site can be found: do not create a similarly named standalone site. Recheck that the group is a Microsoft 365 group and search the SharePoint admin center's Active sites by both the group name and the full committee name. If the site is still not listed, record the group name and leave site setup pending until Microsoft finishes provisioning it. A duplicate would separate mailing-list membership from document access.

Step 2: Confirm Office Staff Are Owners

  1. In the SharePoint admin center, open Sites → Active sites.
  2. Select the committee site.
  3. Select Membership.
  4. Confirm the primary and backup office/admin accounts are Owners or site admins.
  5. Add a backup office/admin owner if needed.
  6. Do not make the committee chair or ordinary committee members Owners.

Owners may edit the home page, navigation, permissions, and site settings. Keep that role with office staff.

Step 3: Give Members Document Access Without Site Editing

Microsoft normally gives group-connected team-site members Edit permission. SHHA uses Contribute so members can work with documents without managing lists or editing the site page.

  1. Open the committee SharePoint site.
  2. Select Settings → Site permissions.
  3. Select Advanced permissions settings.
  4. Select the SharePoint group whose name ends in Members. Do not select Owners or Visitors.
  5. Select Edit User Permissions.
  6. Clear Edit.
  7. Select Contribute.
  8. Select OK.

Do not remove the committee Microsoft 365 group from the site. Group membership keeps the mailing list and document access synchronized.

Step 4: Keep The Site Simple

A team site already includes a default Documents library. Do not create a second Documents library.

  1. Open Documents and confirm it works.
  2. Create a folder named Documents Shared with Board.
  3. If folder colors are available, apply the standard SHHA committee-folder color.
  4. Edit the left navigation and remove unused links. Keep the useful experience limited to Home and Documents.
  5. Do not delete the system Site Pages library; it supports the home page.

Step 5: Make The Home Page Minimal

Only office staff should edit the home page.

  1. From the home page, select Edit.
  2. Use the committee's full name as the title.
  3. Add: “Use the Documents library for committee files and enduring reference materials.”
  4. Add or keep an obvious link to Documents.
  5. Remove unnecessary news, activity, and decorative web parts.
  6. Republish the page.

Step 6: Add The Library To Office OneDrive

This is only for internal office users with SHHA Microsoft accounts. External users should never use OneDrive for committee documents; they use SharePoint in their browser.

  1. Sign in as the office user who needs the shortcut.
  2. Open the committee SharePoint site and then Documents.
  3. Select Add shortcut to OneDrive or Add shortcut to My files.
  4. Open that user's OneDrive and confirm the committee folder appears under My files.
  5. If the desktop OneDrive app is used, confirm the shortcut appears on that computer.
  6. Repeat while signed in as each internal office user who needs the shortcut.

The shortcut points to the group-owned SharePoint library. It does not copy files into a personal OneDrive.

Step 7: Test With An External Member

  1. Ask one existing external group member to open the committee SharePoint site using the same personal email address that received the Microsoft invitation.
  2. Confirm the member can open Documents.
  3. Have the member upload a temporary file named TEST - delete me.
  4. Confirm the member can edit, rename, move, and delete the test file.
  5. Confirm the member cannot edit the home page, navigation, permissions, or membership.
  6. Confirm someone outside the group cannot open the private site.
  7. Remind the external tester to bookmark the SharePoint site and not use OneDrive.

Step 8: Publish The Member Instructions

  1. Send members the Committee SharePoint Guide.
  2. Add the committee mailing list and SharePoint URL to Quick Links & Directory.
  3. Tell external members to bookmark the SharePoint site. Do not give them OneDrive instructions.
  4. Send the matching New Committee Or Task Force or New SharePoint Site For An Existing Committee email.

Final Checklist

  • Existing group-connected site found; no duplicate created
  • Site is Private
  • Office staff are Owners / Full Control
  • Committee members use Contribute permissions
  • Documents library works
  • Documents Shared with Board folder created
  • Home page and navigation simplified
  • Office-user OneDrive shortcuts added separately
  • External member document test passed through SharePoint
  • External member cannot edit the site page
  • Directory updated
  • General member guide sent
  • Matching onboarding email sent

Microsoft References

  • Create a team site in SharePoint
  • Manage sites in the SharePoint admin center
  • Permission levels in SharePoint
  • Add shortcuts to shared folders in OneDrive

Who this is for: the incoming IT professional and staff arranging continuity. Start by obtaining approved individual access through the office, then read the maintained repository guides. This public page explains the systems and responsibilities; credentials, recovery codes, private records and detailed security configuration belong in approved private documentation.

Deployment and address checks: October 13, 2026. Read the current repository status and actual cloud settings before acting; names and migration status can change.

Start with ownership and access

  1. Ask office staff to arrange approved access to the SHHA GitHub organization, Azure subscription, Microsoft 365/Entra administration and the relevant DNS/service-provider accounts. Use your own named accounts.
  2. The repositories are in the Sandia Heights Homeowners Association GitHub organization. The office-accessible sandiahomeowners@gmail.com account is an organization owner; coordinate access and account recovery through the office.
  3. Confirm a primary and backup administrator, billing/renewal owners and recovery contacts for each service. GitHub access does not grant Azure, Microsoft or DNS access.
  4. Keep passwords, API tokens, database connection strings, MFA recovery codes and resident/editorial records out of this wiki and public Git history.

Service accounts and sign-in

SHHA's designated Google account for service ownership is sandiahomeowners@gmail.com (also written Sandiahomeowners@gmail.com). Use Continue with Google and select that account for providers that support it and are linked to the existing SHHA account. This ownership and sign-in instruction was confirmed by SHHA on October 16, 2026; successful access to each provider still needs to be recorded in the private handover register. An email address on an account does not by itself prove that Google sign-in is linked.

For day-to-day administration, use approved individual membership where the provider supports it, while retaining SHHA ownership. Microsoft services and BookStack's Microsoft editing login retain their existing Microsoft identities. Do not create a replacement account, move resources or change authentication just to make a login match this list. If the expected account opens an empty dashboard or asks you to sign up, stop and ask IT Help or office staff to identify the existing account.

Service and entry point What SHHA must retain Sign-in and handover check
Google account, Gmail, Drive and Docs Organizational service ownership and shared documents. Use the designated sandiahomeowners@gmail.com account, subject to the GRIT production-workspace exception below. Keep recovery methods and codes in the approved private register.
GRIT production: Google Drive and Docs The GRIT issue folders, editing templates and production files are in the workspace under shhagrit@gmail.com, as confirmed by SHHA on October 18, 2026. This is an exception to the general designated Google account. This Gmail account is for Google Drive/file-sharing convenience only; do not email it. For editorial correspondence, use griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org. Confirm approved access to this existing workspace through the office/current editor. See the GRIT content flow and editor procedure. Keep account recovery information in the private register.
GRIT ads and source archive: Microsoft OneDrive Office-supplied advertisements and the long-term archive of each issue's complete editable layout package, linked assets, text, approved PDF, and printer proof. Sign in using griteditor@sandiahomeowners.org, as instructed by SHHA. Use this OneDrive access to collect current ads and archive the finished package in the matching year/month folder. Confirm access and the archive location through the Office. See the archive checklist. This Microsoft sign-in is separate from the Google Drive account above.
