GitHub Source repositories, organization ownership, deployment workflows and the public wiki mirror. The office-accessible designated account is recorded as an organization owner. Verify its actual sign-in method and retain named maintainer access and a backup owner.
Azure and Microsoft 365 Application hosting, wiki MySQL/files, GRIT Blob photos, mail, SharePoint and Entra identities. Use authorized Microsoft identities and assigned roles. Google service ownership does not grant subscription or tenant access. Keep the existing Microsoft BookStack login and individual edit attribution.
InMotion The authoritative association-domain DNS documented in the dated DNS section, plus any website/hosting services in the actual account. Confirm the current account, login method, website maintainer and DNS owner through the office. Record any exception to Google sign-in privately.
Vercel The access route to SHHA's Name.com account, plus the earlier GRIT public host and domain configuration while the Azure cutover remains pending. Check the existing team's account and actual sign-in method. Retain access until public hosting, DNS, TLS and rollback requirements are verified. Include Name.com access in any Vercel retirement review.
DigitalOcean Any remaining legacy hosting, reminder workloads and recovery material awaiting retirement review. Confirm ownership and sign-in through the private migration handover. Do not retire resources or restart legacy senders as part of documenting accounts.
Adobe, QuickBooks, Square and other office subscriptions GRIT layout licensing and the office's accounting, sales and payment services. Ask office staff for each existing owner, approved login and billing contact. Do not assume that every office subscription uses Google or the same shared identity. See Systems Inventory.
DAKboard Front office calendar display on a Raspberry Pi 3, with images from SHHA Flickr. Use sandiahomeowners@gmail.com, confirmed by SHHA on November 1, 2026. See Front Office Calendar (DAKboard) for the display and SD-card recovery guide.

Cloudflare's sign-in documentation describes restrictions on linking Google to an existing account; verify the existing login before making changes. For SHHA's Name.com access, start in Vercel as instructed above. A provider's Google button is not proof that it reaches SHHA's existing resources.

Private account handover register

Maintain the full register in an office-approved private location accessible to the primary and backup administrator independently of this wiki server. For every service, record the account or organization, actual sign-in method and owner, named administrators, billing and renewal responsibility, domains/projects it controls, backup location, and the date access and restoration were last checked. Record a protected credential-vault reference and recovery custodian there; keep passwords, tokens, connection strings, payment details, recovery codes and personal recovery contacts out of this public wiki and Git repository.

During handover, open each existing service with the incoming administrator, confirm the expected resources and permissions, and update the private register. Preserve domain renewal access, Google account recovery, Neon data, Azure photo bytes, wiki database/files/configuration and production assets separately. The public Markdown/HTML mirror preserves readable documentation; it cannot recover those accounts or replace full system backups.

Systems and sources of truth

System Responsibility and infrastructure Maintained source
Association website and resident database The website's MariaDB database owns homeowner, property and resident-link records. Authorized website administrators make corrections there. The toolbox and public dashboard use dedicated SELECT-only access; neither is a replacement membership database. Obtain the website maintainer's operating and recovery documentation through the office.
Microsoft 365 Owns mailboxes, calendars, committee groups and SharePoint files. Entra supplies Microsoft identity. The toolbox uses Microsoft Graph for calendar/group reads and approved mail delivery; it does not create a second calendar or change group membership. Microsoft administration and the private toolbox connection/operations guide.
SHHA Toolbox Node.js 24 LTS application on Azure App Service. Platform Microsoft authentication verifies identity; the app enforces separate tool grants. Operational configuration, successful-send history, queued work and authorized private review state persist outside deployed application files. SHHA-toolbox, private, deployment branch main.
Public statistics dashboard Separate Node.js 24 LTS Azure App Service application at dashboard.sandiahomeowners.org. It reads aggregates through SELECT-only queries and generates reports in memory. It has no private staff tools, Graph mail or reminder worker. SHHA-dashboard, private, deployment branch main.
IT wiki Upstream BookStack in an Azure App Service container, with Azure Database for MySQL and persistent Azure Files for configuration/uploads. Public reading and native BookStack Microsoft OIDC editing are separate. Preserve APP_KEY, the database and uploaded files during upgrades or recovery. SHHA-wiki, public. Local project folder: SHHA-wiki. Branch main checks tools and mirrors public content; it does not deploy the BookStack container.
GRIT submissions The public site is sandiaheightsgrit.app. Its domain still served the Vercel-hosted version at this check. The Azure migration version uses Next.js/React on Node.js 22 LTS, Neon PostgreSQL, private Azure Blob photo storage, Cloudflare Turnstile and Resend. Public-domain cutover to Azure remains separate from deploying that version. grit-newsletter, private. Use azure for the Azure deployment; main retains earlier source. Read its deployment guide before choosing a branch.
Neighborhood map Master mapping work is done in QGIS and exported with qgis2web/OpenLayers. GitHub Pages serves the public web export. Its layers and attribute tables are public; the site does not query the homeowner database. Street tiles use OpenStreetMap; aerial imagery uses USGS. Browser filters do not make any published data private. SHHA-map, public, publication branch main. Back up the master QGIS project and source GIS data separately.

The toolbox, dashboard and Azure newsletter version currently share existing Azure compute, with separate applications, settings and deployments. The wiki uses its own plan, database and file storage. Confirm subscriptions, resources, network configuration and current costs in the protected repository/cloud inventory; a public URL or repository name is not a complete deployment specification.

Current addresses and DNS

  • wiki.sandiahomeowners.org: Azure BookStack; anyone can read, approved Microsoft users can edit.
  • dashboard.sandiahomeowners.org: public aggregate dashboard on Azure.
  • toolbox.sandiahomeowners.org: protected staff toolbox with Microsoft login and per-tool grants.
  • sandiaheightsgrit.app: public contribution site; confirm the migration status before changing its host.
  • Neighborhood map on GitHub Pages: current map address; a map subdomain is deferred.

The standalone reminders web address is retired; its function is in Toolbox → Email Reminders. Older toolbox statistics/Board Report links redirect to the separate public dashboard.

InMotion provides the authoritative DNS zone for sandiahomeowners.org at this check; the GRIT domain uses Vercel nameservers. Registrar, DNS provider and application host are different responsibilities. Moving hosting does not require moving nameservers. Preserve mail and unrelated verification records when changing a web destination. Verify the final HTTPS binding/certificate and Microsoft callback, not just the DNS record.

Microsoft login and permission boundaries

The toolbox uses Azure App Service Authentication and its independent group/user grants. A Microsoft sign-in or committee membership does not automatically grant resident-data access. Invited guests can use their own personal email identity in the SHHA tenant without an SHHA email suffix.

BookStack uses its own native OIDC registration and page/role permissions. Do not apply toolbox authentication rules to the wiki: public reading must remain available while edits stay attributed to signed-in people. The GRIT editor uses its own protected editorial access rather than toolbox Microsoft grants.

Retain the existing shared Entra application used by the toolbox and Microsoft Graph when retiring legacy reminder code; an older application name is not evidence it can be deleted. Keep the master calendar/sender admin@sandiahomeowners.org. SHHA display and reminder timezone is America/Denver.

Development, deployment and documentation

  1. Read the project's README, AGENTS.md, deployment and operations guides. Verify the actual deployment branch. Inspect Git status and recent commits; other IT work may share a checkout. Preserve unfinished drafts and do not publish them accidentally.
  2. For Node applications, use the project's declared Node LTS version and committed lockfile. Test with synthetic data. Toolbox/dashboard changes go through their checks and exact Azure deployment; newsletter changes use the Azure branch workflow. A healthy endpoint alone does not verify database, photo, CAPTCHA or email integrations.
  3. For the map, edit the master QGIS source, export outside the repository, use the approved importer, review public fields, then verify GitHub Pages deployment. The website export is not the master GIS backup.
  4. For wiki content, edit the live WYSIWYG page or deliberately send current HTML through BookStack's API. Pull before changing a page, preserve newer human edits and verify live readback. Do not round-trip converted Markdown over rich tables.
  5. The wiki's nightly/on-demand GitHub job exports anonymous public pages as Markdown, rendered HTML and metadata. It makes no BookStack writes and needs no administrator token. Restricted content is omitted from new exports, but previously public content remains in Git history. Maintain private content backups separately.
  6. BookStack software upgrades are separate from content sync. Review the pinned upstream container release, take compatible database/file/configuration backups and plan rollback before applying schema-changing upgrades. Azure deployment CI/CD for the wiki remains work to finish.

Operations and recovery

Azure's current toolbox settings enable email sending, reminder scheduling, group monitoring and group notifications. An authorized administrator should verify Operational status and recent delivery history before relying on a rule or changing automation. This settings check is not a test email or proof that every delivery path works.

The retired reminders address does not establish whether every old hosting workload or scheduler has been shut down. Confirm final state import, successful-send history, the prior scheduler's shutdown and rollback arrangements in the private migration runbook before calling that operational cutover complete. Do not restore an old sending service alongside the current worker.

  • Toolbox deployments must preserve persistent state, send deduplication history, reminder rules, group baselines, queued notices and access policy. Read its private backup rules: some authorized review/campaign files need separate handling rather than entering routine operational backups.
  • Wiki recovery needs MySQL data, configuration/APP_KEY and uploaded-file storage. Markdown/HTML or a portable content ZIP is not a complete installation backup. Full recovery testing remains to be completed.
  • GRIT recovery must cover both Neon records and photo bytes. The current public site and Azure preview share live data; use a separate development database for routine testing. Read the repository's approved migration/integration procedures.
  • Keep an independent recovery copy, document responsible people and test restoration. Confirm master GIS backups, DNS/domain renewals and cloud certificate renewal.

First tasks for the incoming IT professional

  1. Confirm office-assisted access, ownership, backup administrators and service billing/renewal contacts.
  2. Recheck live URLs, private repository guides, deployment branches and cloud settings. Resolve discrepancies between older migration notes and current operation.
  3. Review page visibility and repository visibility together before adding sensitive material. The wiki and its public mirror are not a place for private infrastructure inventories or security-remediation details.
  4. Verify recovery coverage and remaining cutovers, including the GRIT public domain, wiki platform deployment workflow and legacy hosting retirement.
  5. Update this overview with verified completion dates; keep passwords, tenant/resource identifiers, permissions inventories and recovery instructions in the approved private runbooks.

See Public Utilities and SHHA Toolbox for the reader-facing guide and Systems Inventory for the wider software/service list.

Problem What to do
Screen is blank Check the monitor's power and HDMI input, the HDMI cable, and the Raspberry Pi's power. Restart the Pi.

pages.html:
For residents asking to join and office staff handling membership requests. Residents: use one of the request routes below or contact the office. Staff: check the person's request and correct property/unit. Website account access, a membership request, the website's Is Member flag and SHS billing are distinct.

Check existing shared-ownership coverage before treating a household as needing a new membership. Membership from an actual dues-paying property extends to other properties owned or co-owned by people on that property. It does not pass onward through a person connected only to an inherited property. The website’s Is Member flags do not currently capture this extension. See inherited membership and the members-only export limitation.

How membership requests reach the office

  • A resident submits the Account Request form.
  • A resident signs in with a magic link and uses the membership toggle when their address is not marked Member. The form shows Pending, and the request appears under Users → User Queue.
  • A resident contacts the office by phone, email or an in-person visit.

Important exception: a new person may move to an address while its old membership is still marked active. The new person will not get the usual join prompt. Ask them to contact the office explicitly about joining; do not treat the old flag as their consent or billing enrollment.

Queued membership review includes an explicit decision and instructions to coordinate with SHS. A direct property checkbox edit is a separate interface. Neither is confirmation of SHS billing; routine reconciliation is not in place.

Check the membership request queue

When a resident requests membership through the Member Area toggle, the form shows Pending and the request appears under Users → User Queue in the website backend.

  1. Sign in to the website backend with your approved staff account.
  2. Open Users → User Queue and review pending requests.
  3. Check the resident and property/unit, then follow the current office handling below.

Check this queue manually from time to time. Email notification has not been confirmed, so do not rely on an email to alert you. Pending means the request is waiting for review; it does not confirm SHS billing.

Review and decide a queued request

  1. Click the request in Users → User Queue. Check the request type, resident and exact property/unit.
  2. Look for the red MEMBERSHIP REQUESTED notice. It identifies the resident’s request to join.
  3. Coordinate with Sandia Heights Services (SHS) to initiate billing and update the address to reflect the new membership status, as the form instructs.
  4. Under Your Decision, choose the appropriate Approved or Denied option. In the signed-in resident example below, the form says no account decision is required; do not create a duplicate account for that request.
  5. When the intended decision is ready to save, choose Save & Close. Check the saved request decision and the address’s membership status separately. Do not assume that choosing Approved proves SHS billing started or that the address was updated automatically.

Test User at the SHHA office, Unit 3: a demonstration request, not a residential household. The warning tells staff to coordinate billing and update the address. No request decision was changed for this screenshot.

The example’s Approved and Denied controls were left untouched. The logged-in user already has an account. Save & Close was not clicked.

How this differs from changing Is Member directly

The property record also allows a direct Is Member checkbox edit. That is a different interface from the queued request’s explicit Approved/Denied review. A property flag alone does not show that staff reviewed the queued request or coordinated with SHS.

What is not currently tracked

The queue provides a website decision, but there is no separate recorded follow-up confirming that SHS billing started, and no routine audit or reconciliation against SHS records. The website’s Is Member flag and a saved Approved decision do not establish that SHS received a billing request or started billing.

Finding information about a new member

Evidence of requests and communications with SHS is in the office inbox. Search the relevant correspondence for the person and property/unit. Review the website’s Users → User Queue request/decision and property record separately from correspondence with SHS. There is no separate recorded follow-up establishing that billing began. A sent request or the Is Member flag alone is not confirmation of SHS billing.

Resident names, request details, billing evidence and follow-up notes belong in approved private systems, not in this public wiki.

For instructions residents can follow, use Update your resident information and preferences.

Need help? Contact office@sandiahomeowners.org for resident records and membership, or IT Help for technical access. Return to the Staff guide.

Continue with membership and outreach

  • Understand inherited memberships before interpreting multi-property groups or choosing an outreach audience.
  • Use Welcome Visits for household outreach to assign volunteers and record packet preparation and delivery.

pages.html:
For office staff, membership volunteers and administrators reviewing owners with more than one property. Start in Addresses & people → Advanced → Quick checks → Owners & accounts → Ownership & membership.

SHHA’s shared ownership membership rule

SHHA uses shared ownership for membership coverage. Anyone on a dues-paying property extends membership to other properties they own or co-own. Those additional properties have inherited membership; their complete co-owner lists do not have to be identical. Coverage must come from an actual dues-paying property; it does not pass onward through a co-owner whose connection is only to an inherited property.

Which property pays dues matters

Alice owns A. Alice and Bob co-own B. Bob owns C.

Actual dues-paying propertyCoverageReason
A, owned by AliceA pays; B inherits; C is not covered by A’s payment.Alice’s payment extends to B. Bob’s connection to inherited B does not extend that coverage to C.
B, co-owned by Alice and BobB pays; A and C both inherit.Both Alice and Bob are on the dues-paying property, so coverage extends to the other properties each owns or co-owns.

Why a website members-only export is incomplete

The website does not currently apply shared-ownership coverage. It records each property’s Is Member flag; the ownership comparison views are in Toolbox. A property absent from a members-only export may still be covered through shared ownership.

As of November 18, 2026, SHHA estimates that exporting only website members misses roughly 100 properties under this membership definition. This is an approximate coverage estimate, not an audited count of dues payments. Check shared ownership before classifying an address as uncovered or choosing an outreach audience.

Toolbox comparison definitions

Use Shared ownership as the starting comparison, then check the actual dues-paying source within each group. The tool can group a chain more broadly than SHHA’s coverage rule. It retains Individual properties and Identical ownership as alternative comparisons; no comparison result updates website records or verifies SHS billing.

DefinitionWhat it groupsSeparate comparison example
Individual propertiesEach property is a separate membership unit.Counts X, Y and Z as three separate units.
Identical ownershipProperties group only when their complete lists of linked owners match.Alice owns X and Y. Alice and Bob own Z. X and Y group together; Z stays separate: two units.
Shared ownershipProperties group through a common linked owner, including connected chains of co-owners.The same X, Y and Z group together through Alice: one unit.

The practical difference is often an extra co-owner: “Alice” and “Alice + Bob” are different complete owner lists for Identical ownership, but share Alice for Shared ownership.

The tool’s Shared ownership comparison can join the whole A–B–C chain above. Apply SHHA’s actual coverage rule within that group: C does not inherit when only A pays dues; C does inherit when jointly owned B is the dues-paying property. A connected group alone is not a coverage or billing decision.

Read the two inherited counts carefully

  • Inherited memberships is the selected scenario’s count of properties beyond one per group. It can include groups with no property currently marked Member. It is not a count of newly enrolled or paying members. Apply the dues-paying-source check before treating a grouped property as covered.
  • Possible inherited properties / count identifies properties not marked Member in a group that also contains a property marked Member. These are review candidates; a current Member flag is not billing evidence.

Review a group before outreach or changes

  1. Select Shared ownership to review the chosen membership rule. Read Details for the definition and example; the other definitions remain available for comparison.
  2. Review Owners, All properties & membership, Already marked Member, Possible inherited properties and Possible inherited count.
  3. With Identical ownership or Shared ownership selected, use Only possible inherited memberships to narrow to groups with a recorded Member property and another property not marked Member. Leave it unchecked to see all multi-property groups, including groups whose properties are all marked Member or none are. This checkbox is hidden for Individual properties, which has no inheritance grouping.
  4. Check the actual linked owner accounts and address/unit. Matching names do not establish that two accounts are the same person.
  5. Identify the actual dues-paying property and the person’s connection to it, then check their ownership or co-ownership of each additional property. Do not extend coverage through someone whose only connection is to an inherited property. Resolve uncertain ownership or billing with the office. Use the membership request and review process for a real enrollment request.

Choosing a definition changes the comparison, not dues, property flags, resident links or GRIT delivery. A property whose previous household’s Member flag remains on is a separate record-review issue; it can hide the new resident’s join prompt. See membership requests and tracking.

For welcoming a household, continue to Welcome Visits. For a confusing ownership or billing case, contact office staff. For tool access, contact IT Help.

pages.html:
For office staff and welcoming volunteers with approved Welcome Visits access. Open Welcome Visits from SHHA Toolbox. If access is restricted, ask office staff or IT Help. The tool tracks household welcome work separately from membership enrollment and SHS billing.

Find the right household

  1. Wait for the list to load. Use Refresh list when you need current website information.
  2. Choose Show. All visits & history includes delivered entries; To visit hides delivered entries. Use Needs a volunteer or Assigned visits for assignment work.
  3. Search by address, name or volunteer. Check the unit and incoming household, not just the street number.
  4. Choose the Arrival period and date order. The default period is the past 12 months; use Choose dates… for a specific range.
  5. Use Display & more options for resident type, date details and fields. New tenants can appear in the main visit list even while the owner remains linked. Unconfirmed owner additions are under Person added / co-owners.

Understand the arrival date and membership label

  • Recorded occupancy comes from the website’s recorded ownership/occupancy start.
  • Estimated arrival uses resident/address association dates. Account creation is a fallback when a link date is missing. Neither proves a move-in date.
  • Person added / move-in unconfirmed calls for review; a new account or added co-owner does not by itself establish a new household.
  • A committee-entered move-in date takes priority. Review Move-in dates when saved and website dates differ.

Membership colors and Other properties show website records. They do not confirm payment or automatically determine visit eligibility. Before treating a household as uncovered, check whether membership extends from an actual dues-paying property through shared ownership. A connection only to an inherited property does not extend coverage onward to another co-owner’s properties. The website’s property flag does not currently capture that extension. Use SHHA’s inherited membership rule for multi-property questions and membership requests and tracking for enrollment.

Record the welcome work

  1. Set the Volunteer and add useful Notes. Use Save edit when the tool shows an unsaved edit; confirm it saved for the committee.
  2. Mark Packet created only when the welcome packet is prepared.
  3. Mark Delivered only after delivery. Packet creation and delivery are independent; one does not establish the other.
  4. If a visit is not needed, use the rightmost No visit needed checkbox. The entry moves to Show → No visit needed; assignments, checks and notes are retained.
  5. To restore that entry, use Undo in the notice or uncheck it under No visit needed. This decision applies to the entry, not every later household at the address.

Checkbox changes save shared committee work. Read the save confirmation or error; do not assume a failed save reached other volunteers. Ask the committee lead or office if the household, visit need or packet type is uncertain.

Use the meeting and packet views

Meeting view collapses resident details and history for discussion. Confirm the household’s homeowner/tenant bag label. Use Bag PDF or Cover PDF for one household and check the address and HOA Unit before preparing the packet.

Copy view, Print list and CSV can include contact details and notes even when those fields are collapsed on screen. Keep these outputs in approved private committee storage and communication channels.

Finished? Check the volunteer, preparation/delivery state and notes for the correct household. A delivered welcome packet does not complete membership enrollment. Send membership intent to the office through the membership request process.

For source record corrections, use property ownership changes or manual resident and tenant additions. Do not create another ownership change just to give a tenant an arrival date. For help, contact office staff or IT Help.
